A state statute provides financial aid for tuition, books, and other academic materials to students who are accepted into one of the state's universities. The state statute lists several requirements for a student to receive this financial aid. One of the requirements is that the student be a citizen of the United States or a resident noncitizen who has applied for citizenship.
A teenager was accepted into one of the state's universities and applied for financial aid pursuant to the state statute. However, his application was denied solely because he is a resident noncitizen who has not applied for United States citizenship. The teenager filed suit in federal court to challenge the constitutionality of the state statute's provision relating to United States citizenship.
Will the federal court likely find the provision to be constitutional?

A state enacted a statute that prohibited children born outside of marriage from receiving welfare benefits that the state provides to children who live in households below the federal poverty line. The purpose of the statute was to encourage individuals to get married before having children.
A man and his unmarried partner had a daughter out of wedlock. Before the man and his partner married, the partner died. The man's annual household income was below the federal poverty line, so he applied for welfare benefits on the daughter's behalf. The state agency overseeing the program denied the application based on the state statute.
The man filed suit in a federal district court, alleging that the state statute violates the equal protection clause.
Which of the following best states the burden of persuasion in the suit?

The legislature of State B enacted a statute requiring that all law enforcement officers in that state be United States citizens. A lawfully admitted noncitizen became a permanent resident five years before the enactment of this statute. He sought employment as a forensic pathologist in the state coroner's office. He was denied that job solely because he was not a citizen. The resident noncitizen thereupon brought suit in federal district court against appropriate state officials seeking to invalidate this citizenship requirement on federal constitutional grounds.
Which of the following is the strongest ground upon which to attack this citizenship requirement?

A city ordinance prohibits any type of protesting on the public sidewalks immediately in front of any abortion clinic during the one hour before and one hour after the clinic's business hours. The purpose of the ordinance is to allow a clinic's staff to safely arrive at the beginning and leave at the end of their workdays, ensuring that the clinic could consistently operate with a full staff.
A man's wife recently died from a fatal infection caused by negligence during a procedure at an improperly staffed abortion clinic. One morning, the man sat on the sidewalk in front of the abortion clinic one hour before it opened until one hour after the clinic closed, crying silently and holding a large sign that read, "Do your jobs!" The man was prosecuted for violating the ordinance. The man has claimed that the ordinance is unconstitutional as applied to him.
Is the man likely to succeed?

A state law prohibits dentists from advertising themselves as "certified dental specialists" unless they are certified by the American Dental Association (ADA) to practice the stated specialty. The state legislature passed the law to combat misleading dentist advertisements because many consumers consider ADA certification when selecting a dental provider. A dentist whose practice is limited to implant dentistry, a specialty that is not recognized by the ADA, has challenged the law as a violation of the First Amendment free speech clause.
Which of the following is the best argument that the state can advance for upholding this law?

A state law provides that only U.S. citizens may serve as jurors in the state courts of that state. A woman who is a lawful resident noncitizen and who has resided in the state for many years was summoned for jury duty in a state court. The woman's name was selected from a list of potential jurors that was compiled from a comprehensive list of local residents. She was disqualified from service solely because she is not a U.S. citizen.
The woman has filed an action for a declaratory judgment that the state law is unconstitutional.
Who should prevail in this action?

A state law increased the minimum hourly wage that employers are required to pay their employees by 12 percent. The law was enacted to address a variety of economic problems in the state, including the substantial need to pay persons a living wage. The owner of a retail store was assessed a fine for violating the law. The owner sincerely believes that God does not want him to increase the minimum hourly wage he pays his employees because a person's increase in wealth should result from an increase in faith as opposed to governmental action.
Is the law unconstitutional as applied to the owner?

A state prohibits voting for a write-in candidate in both primary and general elections. However, the state provides a mechanism by which individuals who want to appear as candidates on the primary ballot, as well as groups that want to be classified as a party, can do so.
Of the following, which is the best argument that a voter challenging the constitutionality of this ban on write-in candidates can make?

A man, who is a resident noncitizen, applied for employment as a state trooper with the state highway patrol. After the man passed a psychological examination and completed the requisite training courses, he was denied employment. The state highway patrol agency explained that the man was ineligible for employment as a state trooper pursuant to a policy that the agency had enacted six months prior. The policy disqualifies all noncitizens from employment with the state highway patrol, restricting employment to U.S. citizens.
The man has filed an action for a declaratory judgment that the agency's policy is unconstitutional as applied to him.
Which of the following best states the burden of persuasion in this action?

A county school board has adopted a program that will hire teachers to teach English to elementary school students whose primary language is not English. The teachers will be employed by the school board and assigned to all public and private schools within the county. Most of the private schools in the county are faith-based, so the program has adopted procedures to ensure that the teachers are not involved in religious instruction. The number of teachers allocated to each school will be based solely on the number of nonnative English-speakers enrolled at the school.
Does the program likely violate the establishment clause of the First Amendment?

Congress enacted a federal statute that awards funds to nongovernmental organizations in the United States and around the world to combat the spread of a deadly airborne virus. The statute requires that the funds be used strictly for research and testing related to the virus. The last section of the statute conditions the award of the funds on the recipient's agreement to publicly announce its support for free-trade policies.
A U.S. nongovernmental organization that is headquartered abroad qualifies for funding under the federal statute. The organization does not want to publicly support free-trade policies because it believes that such support will alienate certain foreign governments with which the organization works. As a result, the organization has filed suit in federal court, seeking a declaratory judgment that the statute's condition requiring the announcement of support for free-trade policies compels speech and is therefore unconstitutional as applied to it.
How should the court rule?

After a university's hockey team beat its biggest crosstown rival, the university's students caused over $100,000 in property damage in the neighborhood surrounding the university's campus while celebrating their school's victory. The city council determined that it could reduce future property damage in the neighborhood by lowering the number of students living off-campus in the neighborhood. By a unanimous vote, the city council passed an ordinance that limited the number of residents in any apartment in the city to two people per bedroom.
A family of five seeking to rent a two-bedroom apartment in the city has sued to challenge the constitutionality of the city ordinance.
Is the city ordinance constitutional?

A city ordinance requires residents to keep firearms unloaded and disassembled while the firearms are located in their homes. The ordinance also requires residents to keep the disassembled firearm parts and any ammunition in separate safes. The purpose of the ordinance is to deter gun ownership by making it inconvenient to store firearms.
A resident of the city who owns and keeps firearms in her home for self-defense has filed suit against the city in a federal district court, arguing that the ordinance is unconstitutional.
Is the ordinance constitutional?

A state legislature enacted a statute that allowed executors to claim a tax deduction for the sale of securities that were purchased by an estate after the decedent's death. After the statute was enacted, the state suffered a significant decrease in revenue because the number of estates that claimed the tax deduction was greater than originally projected. To recover this lost revenue, the legislature amended the statute to prevent an estate from claiming the deduction unless the decedent owned the securities prior to death. The amendment was made retroactive so that its effective date was when the statute was initially enacted.
Before the amendment was enacted, an executor sold securities that he had purchased for a decedent's estate after her death. The executor attempted to claim the tax deduction on the estate's tax returns but the state agency that processes tax returns denied his claim even though the estate had purchased the securities before the amendment was enacted. The executor has filed suit against the agency to challenge the constitutionality of the retroactive application of the amendment.
Is the executor's suit likely to succeed?

A state-funded hospital offered free and low-cost medical procedures to indigent patients, regardless of residency status. Following an influx of new patients from neighboring states requesting free or low-cost medical treatment, the state enacted a new law prohibiting state-funded hospitals from providing free or low-cost medical procedures to any patient who has not resided in the state for at least six months.
An indigent man moved to the state four months ago. He sought to undergo a medical procedure at the state-funded hospital but was denied due to the state's durational residency requirement. The man sued to invalidate the state law that limits access to free or low-cost medical procedures based on residency.
Should the man prevail in his action?

questions.question:
A city ordinance makes the city building inspector responsible for ensuring that all buildings in that city are kept up to building code standards and requires the inspector to refer for prosecution all known building code violations. Another ordinance provides that the city building inspector may be discharged for "good cause." The building inspector took a newspaper reporter through a number of run-down buildings in a slum neighborhood. After using various epithets and slurs to describe the occupants of these buildings, the building inspector stated to the reporter: "I do not even try to get these buildings up to code or to have their owners prosecuted for code violations because if these buildings are repaired, the people who live in them will just wreck them again." The reporter published these statements in a story in the local newspaper. The building inspector admitted he made the statements.
On the basis of these statements, the city council discharged the building inspector.
Is the action of the city council constitutional?

choices.a: No, because the statements were lawful comments on a matter of public concern.
choices.b: No, because the statements were published in a newspaper that is protected by the First and Fourteenth Amendments.
choices.c: Yes, because the building inspector is a government employee and a person holding such a position may not make public comments inconsistent with current governmental policy.
choices.d: Yes, because the statements demonstrate that the building inspector has an attitude toward a certain class of persons that interferes with the proper performance of the obligations of his job.

Q82071

A city ordinance makes the city building inspector responsible for ensuring that all buildings in that city are kept up to building code standards and requires the inspector to refer for prosecution all known building code violations. Another ordinance provides that the city building inspector may be discharged for "good cause." The building inspector took a newspaper reporter through a number of run-down buildings in a slum neighborhood. After using various epithets and slurs to describe the occupants of these buildings, the building inspector stated to the reporter: "I do not even try to get these buildings up to code or to have their owners prosecuted for code violations because if these buildings are repaired, the people who live in them will just wreck them again." The reporter published these statements in a story in the local newspaper. The building inspector admitted he made the statements.

On the basis of these statements, the city council discharged the building inspector.

Is the action of the city council constitutional?

一项城市法令规定，城市建筑监察员负责确保该市所有建筑都符合建筑规范标准，并要求监察员将所有已知的建筑规范违规行为移交起诉。另一项法令规定，城市建筑监察员可因“正当理由”被解雇。该建筑监察员带领一名报社记者参观了贫民区的一些破旧建筑。在用各种侮辱性绰号和诽谤言辞形容这些建筑的居住者后，该建筑监察员向记者表示：“我根本不打算让这些建筑达到规范标准，也不打算让它们的业主因违反规范而受到起诉，因为如果这些建筑被修复，住在里面的人只会再次破坏它们。”记者在当地报纸的一篇报道中发表了这些言论。该建筑监察员承认他发表了这些言论。

基于这些言论，市议会解雇了该建筑监察员。

市议会的行为是否合宪？
options:
A. No, because the statements were lawful comments on a matter of public concern.
不合宪，因为这些言论是对公众关切事务的合法评论。

B. No, because the statements were published in a newspaper that is protected by the First and Fourteenth Amendments.
不合宪，因为这些言论发表在受 First and Fourteenth Amendments 保护的报纸上。

C. Yes, because the building inspector is a government employee and a person holding such a position may not make public comments inconsistent with current governmental policy.
合宪，因为该建筑监察员是政府雇员，担任此类职位的人不得发表与现行政府政策不一致的公开评论。

D. Yes, because the statements demonstrate that the building inspector has an attitude toward a certain class of persons that interferes with the proper performance of the obligations of his job.
合宪，因为这些言论表明该建筑监察员对某一类人群的态度妨碍了其正常履行工作职责。
data.explanation:
Acceptance of public employment does not eliminate an individual's right to free speech - but this right is not absolute. When a public employee is speaking as a private citizen, the government can limit that speech if its interest in efficient government function outweighs the employee's right to free speech. And when the employee is speaking pursuant to official duties (ie, within the scope of employment), the government has even greater latitude to regulate that speech and First Amendment protections rarely apply.

Here, the city building inspector was likely speaking as a private citizen since talking to a reporter presumably fell outside his official duties. But since the inspector's statements showed his lack of effort to get some buildings up to code, the city council's interest in ensuring that he properly perform his job outweighed his right to free speech. And if talking to reporters was an official duty, the city council's right to regulate that speech was even greater. Therefore, the city's decision to discharge him was constitutional.

(Choice A) Comments on a matter of public concern (as seen here) are afforded greater First Amendment protection than those involving a private concern. But the city council still had "good cause" to fire the inspector since his statements demonstrated that he could not properly perform his job.

(Choice B) The First Amendment (applied to the states through the Fourteenth Amendment) gives the media the right to publish information on matters of public concern. But the fact that the inspector's statements were published in a newspaper is irrelevant to determining whether the city council can fire him for those statements.

(Choice C) A government employee can make public comments that are inconsistent with current government policy if those comments do not interfere with his/her ability to adequately perform official duties.

Educational objective: When a public employee is speaking as a private citizen, the government can only restrict that speech if its interest in efficient government function outweighs the employee's right to free speech. But when the employee is speaking pursuant to official duties, the government has greater latitude to regulate that speech.



选项正确率统计：A选项 5%，B选项 1%，C选项 19%，D选项 73%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

接受公职并不意味着个人言论自由权的丧失——但这项权利并非绝对。当公职人员以私人公民身份发言时，如果政府在高效运作方面的利益超过了雇员的言论自由权，政府可以限制该言论。而当雇员根据其官方职责（即在雇佣范围内）发言时，政府在规制该言论方面拥有更大的自由度，First Amendment 的保护很少适用。

在此案中，该市建筑监察员很可能是以私人公民身份发言，因为与记者交谈据推测超出了他的官方职责范围。但由于监察员的言论表明他并未尽力使某些建筑达到规范标准，因此市议会在确保其正常履行工作职责方面的利益超过了他的言论自由权。并且，如果与记者交谈是一项官方职责，市议会规制该言论的权利就更大了。因此，市政府解雇他的决定是合宪的。

（选项 A） 对公众关切事务的评论（如此处所示）比涉及私人关切的评论受到更强的 First Amendment 保护。但市议会仍有“正当理由”解雇该监察员，因为他的言论表明他无法正常履行其工作职责。

（选项 B） First Amendment（通过 Fourteenth Amendment 适用于各州）赋予媒体发布有关公众关切事务信息的权利。但监察员的言论发表在报纸上这一事实，与确定市议会是否可以因此解雇他无关。

（选项 C） 如果政府雇员的公开评论不妨碍其充分履行官方职责的能力，那么他可以发表与现行政府政策不一致的公开评论。

教学目标：当公职人员以私人公民身份发言时，只有在政府于高效运作方面的利益超过雇员的言论自由权时，政府才能限制该言论。但当雇员根据其官方职责发言时，政府在规制该言论方面拥有更大的自由度。

References

Pickering v. Bd. of Educ., 391 U.S. 563, 568 (1968) (explaining that a public employee's right to free speech as a private citizen must be balanced against the government's interest in efficient government function).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law / First Amendment
正确答案
选项 D (Yes)
合宪，因为言论表明其态度妨碍了工作职责的履行。
核心考点：公职人员言论自由

本题考察的是政府雇员（Public Employee）的言论自由权与政府作为雇主维持高效运作（Efficient Government Function）之间的平衡。

适用的法律标准通常被称为 Pickering Balancing Test（皮克林平衡测试）：

  1. 第一步：雇员是否就“公众关切的事项”（Matter of Public Concern）发言？
  2. 第二步：如果是，法院必须权衡雇员的言论利益与政府促进公共服务效率的利益。
本题逻辑分析

虽然建筑监察员谈论的是贫民窟建筑状况（属于公众关切事项），但他的言论内容不仅是观点表达，更是承认了渎职。

他明确表示：“我根本不打算让这些建筑达到规范标准...”（I do not even try...）。

关键点：当言论直接证明雇员拒绝履行核心职责（Insubordination or neglect of duty）时，政府维持机构正常运作的利益压倒了雇员的言论自由权。

因此，市议会有“正当理由”（Good Cause）解雇他，这不违反宪法。

为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A：错误
虽然言论确实涉及“公众关切”，但这并不是绝对的护身符。如果言论本身证明了雇员不称职（Incompetence），政府仍可解雇他。
选项 B：错误
媒体发布（Published in a newspaper）并不改变雇佣关系的本质。First Amendment 保护报纸发布的权利，但不豁免雇员因承认渎职而承担的后果。
选项 C：错误
这个选项太绝对了。公职人员可以批评政府政策（例如：“我认为这个建筑法规不合理”），只要这种批评不导致工作场所的混乱或妨碍履职。本题的关键在于他拒绝执行政策，而不仅仅是口头反对。
💡 MBE 考试技巧

在处理 Public Employee Speech 问题时，请遵循以下思维路径：

  1. 如果是履行职务时的发言（Official Duties）👉 无 First Amendment 保护（政府可随意监管）。
  2. 如果是作为公民发言（Citizen）：
    • 看是否干扰了工作（Disruption/Interference）。
    • 本题中，"I do not even try" = 承认不工作 = 极大的干扰。

questions.question:
An independent municipal water-supply district was incorporated under the applicable laws of a state. The district was created solely to supply water to an entirely new community in a recently developed area of the state. That new community is racially, ethnically, and socioeconomically diverse, and the community has never engaged in any discrimination against members of minority groups.
The five-member elected governing board of the newly created water-supply district contains two persons who are members of racial minority groups. At its first meeting, the governing board adopted a rule unqualifiedly setting aside 25% of all positions on the staff of the water-supply district and 25% of all contracts to be awarded by the district to members of racial minority groups. The purpose of the rule was "to help redress the historical discrimination against these groups in this country and to help them achieve economic parity with other groups in our society." Assume that no federal statute applies.
In a suit by appropriate parties challenging the constitutionality of these set-asides, what is the most appropriate ruling based on applicable United States Supreme Court precedent?

choices.a: The set-asides are constitutional, because the function and activities of the water-supply district are of a proprietary nature rather than a governmental nature and, therefore, are not subject to the usual requirements of the Fourteenth Amendment.
choices.b: The set-asides are constitutional, because they would assure members of racial minority groups the equal protection of the laws.
choices.c: The set-asides are unconstitutional, because they would deny other potential employees or potential contractors the equal protection of the laws.
choices.d: The set-asides are unconstitutional, because they would impermissibly impair the right to contract of other potential employees or potential contractors.

In a suit by appropriate parties challenging the constitutionality of these set-asides, what is the most appropriate ruling based on applicable United States Supreme Court precedent?

一个独立的市政供水区根据某州的适用法律成立。该供水区的设立完全是为了向该州一个新开发区内的全新社区供水。该新社区在种族、民族和社会经济上是多元化的，且该社区从未对少数族裔成员进行过任何歧视。

新成立的供水区的五人选举制管理委员会中有两名成员是少数族裔。在其第一次会议上，该管理委员会通过了一项规定，无条件地为少数族裔成员保留供水区员工总职位的25%以及该区将授予的所有合同的25%。该规定的目的是“帮助纠正本国历史上对这些群体的歧视，并帮助他们在我们的社会中实现与其他群体的经济平等。”假设没有联邦法规适用。

在相关方提起诉讼，质疑这些保留份额措施的合宪性时，根据适用的美国最高法院判例，最恰当的裁决是什么？
options:
A. The set-asides are constitutional, because the function and activities of the water-supply district are of a proprietary nature rather than a governmental nature and, therefore, are not subject to the usual requirements of the Fourteenth Amendment.
该保留份额措施是合宪的，因为供水区的职能和活动是所有权性质而非政府性质，因此不受第十四修正案常规要求的约束。

B. The set-asides are constitutional, because they would assure members of racial minority groups the equal protection of the laws.
该保留份额措施是合宪的，因为它们将确保少数族裔群体获得法律的平等保护。

C. The set-asides are unconstitutional, because they would deny other potential employees or potential contractors the equal protection of the laws.
该保留份额措施是违宪的，因为它们将剥夺其他潜在雇员或潜在承包商受法律平等保护的权利。

D. The set-asides are unconstitutional, because they would impermissibly impair the right to contract of other potential employees or potential contractors.
该保留份额措施是违宪的，因为它们将不被允许地损害其他潜在雇员或潜在承包商的合同权。
data.explanation:
Permissible race-based affirmative action


SCOTUS precedentDiscriminatory actionGovernment interest
Richmond v. J.A. Croson Co.Minority set-asides for government employment/contractsRemedying its own history of racial discrimination
Freeman v. PittsRace-based student assignments in public elementary/high schoolsRemedying past intentional racial segregation in public schools
Grutter v. BollingerRace-based admissions policy in state universitiesAchieving diverse student body in higher education
SCOTUS = Supreme Court of the United States

All race-based classifications imposed by the government are subject to strict scrutiny under the equal protection clause - even when those classifications are designed to promote racial equality. That is because race is a suspect class that has historically faced discrimination. As a result, the government must prove that its racially discriminatory actions are necessary to achieve a compelling government interest.

Here, the water-district board developed an affirmative action program that sets aside a percentage of its employment positions and contracts for racial minorities (ie, minority set-asides). And in Richmond v. J.A. Croson Co. , the Supreme Court held that these discriminatory programs can only survive strict scrutiny if the government proves that:
  • it has a compelling interest in remedying its own history of discrimination against the favored group and
  • the discriminatory program is necessary because race-neutral methods are unavailable or insufficient to further that interest.
But since the water-district board created this program to address the country's broader history of discrimination against racial minority groups - not its own specific history of racial discrimination - the board's set-asides cannot survive strict scrutiny. Therefore, the most appropriate ruling is that the set-asides are unconstitutional because they would deny other (non-minority) potential employees and contractors the equal protection of the laws.

(Choice A) All state and municipal actions - whether proprietary or governmental in nature - must comply with the Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause.

(Choice B) The set-asides do not assure racial minority groups the equal protection of the laws. Instead, they prefer racial minority groups and deny other potential employees and contractors the equal protection of the laws.

(Choice D) The contracts clause of the U.S. Constitution restricts state and municipal legislatures' ability to impair existing contracts. But actions that affect future contracts (as seen here) are not subject to this clause.

Educational objective: All race-based classifications imposed by the government must survive strict scrutiny. This requires the government to prove that these classifications are necessary to achieve a compelling government interest - eg, to remedy its own history of racial discrimination.

允许的基于种族的平权行动


最高法院判例歧视性行为政府利益
Richmond v. J.A. Croson Co.为政府雇佣/合同设立的少数族裔保留份额纠正其自身的种族歧视历史
Freeman v. Pitts公立中小学中基于种族的学生分配纠正过去在公立学校中故意的种族隔离
Grutter v. Bollinger州立大学中基于种族的招生政策在高等教育中实现学生群体的多样性
SCOTUS = 美国最高法院

所有由政府实施的基于种族的分类都必须根据平等保护条款接受严格审查——即使这些分类旨在促进种族平等。这是因为种族是一个在历史上曾面临歧视的可疑分类。因此，政府必须证明其种族歧视行为对于实现紧迫的政府利益是必要的。

在此案中，供水区管理委员会制定了一项平权行动计划，为少数族裔保留一定比例的雇佣职位和合同（即少数族裔保留份额）。在 Richmond v. J.A. Croson Co. 案中，最高法院裁定，这些歧视性计划只有在政府证明以下情况时才能通过严格审查：
  • 政府在纠正其自身对受优待群体的歧视历史方面具有紧迫利益，并且
  • 该歧视性计划是必要的，因为不存在或不足以推进该利益的种族中立方法。
但由于供水区管理委员会设立此计划是为了解决国家更广泛的针对少数族裔的歧视历史——而非其自身特定的种族歧视历史——该委员会的保留份额措施无法通过严格审查。因此，最恰当的裁决是，该保留份额措施是违宪的，因为它们将剥夺其他（非少数族裔）潜在雇员和承包商受法律平等保护的权利。

（选项A）所有州和市的行为——无论是所有权性质还是政府性质——都必须遵守第十四修正案的平等保护条款。

（选项B）该保留份额措施并非确保少数族裔群体获得法律的平等保护。相反，它们优待了少数族裔群体，并剥夺了其他潜在雇员和承包商受法律平等保护的权利。

（选项D）美国宪法的合同条款限制了州和市立立法机构损害现有合同的能力。但影响未来合同的行为（如此案所示）不受此条款的约束。

教学目的：所有由政府实施的基于种族的分类都必须通过严格审查。这要求政府证明这些分类对于实现紧迫的政府利益是必要的——例如，为了纠正其自身的种族歧视历史。

References

U.S. Const. amend. XIV (equal protection clause).

Richmond v. J.A. Croson Co., 488 U.S. 469, 504 (1989) (holding that racially-based set-asides for government employment or contracts must satisfy strict scrutiny).

MBE 考点解析

Equal Protection & Affirmative Action
⚖️ 核心原则：严格审查 (Strict Scrutiny)

根据第十四修正案的平等保护条款 (Equal Protection Clause)，所有基于种族 (Race) 的政府分类——即使是旨在帮助少数族裔的“平权行动” (Affirmative Action)——都必须接受严格审查。

政府必须证明该措施是：

  1. 为了实现紧迫的政府利益 (Compelling Government Interest)；且
  2. 手段是必要的 (Necessary) 或狭义剪裁的 (Narrowly Tailored)。
📚 关键判例：Richmond v. J.A. Croson Co.

美国最高法院在该案中明确指出：

仅仅为了纠正“广泛的社会性歧视” (Societal Discrimination) 而设立的种族配额是违宪的。

州或地方政府只有在纠正其自身过去的具体歧视行为时，才具有“紧迫的政府利益”。

第一步 识别事实

题目中强调：这是一个新成立的供水区，服务于一个新社区，且该社区从未有过歧视历史。

第二步 应用规则

供水区设立 25% 的种族保留份额 (Set-asides)，目的是解决“本国历史上的歧视” (Historical discrimination in this country)。

由于该机构没有自身的歧视历史需要纠正，它缺乏通过严格审查所需的“紧迫政府利益”。试图解决国家层面的历史遗留问题超出了地方政府的权限范围。

结论 判定结果

因此，该措施违反了平等保护条款。正确答案是 C。

🚫 为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A (Proprietary Nature):
错误。无论是行使政府职能还是所有权职能 (Proprietary function)，州和地方政府的行为都必须遵守宪法。没有“商业行为例外”可以豁免第十四修正案。
选项 B (Assure Equal Protection):
错误。这种配额制实际上是基于种族的分类，它剥夺了非少数族裔申请人的平等竞争机会，而不是“确保”平等保护。
选项 D (Right to Contract):
错误。合同条款 (Contracts Clause) 仅限制政府损害现有合同的义务，而不限制政府制定影响未来合同的规则。
💡 MBE 考试技巧
看到“种族配额 (Set-asides)” + “地方政府” + “纠正社会普遍歧视”， 几乎总是违宪的。
只有纠正该特定实体过去具体的歧视才可能合宪。

questions.question:
A state statute provides financial aid for tuition, books, and other academic materials to students who are accepted into one of the state's universities. The state statute lists several requirements for a student to receive this financial aid. One of the requirements is that the student be a citizen of the United States or a resident noncitizen who has applied for citizenship.
A teenager was accepted into one of the state's universities and applied for financial aid pursuant to the state statute. However, his application was denied solely because he is a resident noncitizen who has not applied for United States citizenship. The teenager filed suit in federal court to challenge the constitutionality of the state statute's provision relating to United States citizenship.
Will the federal court likely find the provision to be constitutional?

choices.a: No, because the state likely cannot show that the provision is necessary to achieve a compelling government interest.
choices.b: No, because this type of arbitrary classification is barred by the Article IV privileges and immunities clause.
choices.c: Yes, because the Fourteenth Amendment does not apply to resident noncitizens.
choices.d: Yes, because the provision is reasonably related to a legitimate state interest.

questions.question:
A city owns and operates a large public auditorium. It leases the auditorium to any group that wishes to use it for a meeting, lecture, concert, or contest. Each user must post a damage deposit and pay rent, which is calculated only for the actual time the building is used by the lessee. Reservations are made on a first-come, first-served basis.
A private organization that permits only males to serve in its highest offices rented the auditorium for its national convention. The organization planned to install its new officers at that convention. It broadly publicized the event, inviting members of the general public to attend the installation ceremony at the city auditorium. No statute or administrative rule prohibits the organization from restricting its highest offices to men.
An appropriate plaintiff sues the private organization seeking to enjoin it from using the city auditorium for the installation of its new officers. The sole claim of the plaintiff is that the use of this auditorium by the organization for the installation ceremony violates the Fourteenth Amendment because the organization disqualifies women from serving in its highest offices.
Will the plaintiff prevail?

choices.a: No, because the freedom of association protected by the Fourteenth Amendment prohibits the city from interfering in any way with the organization's use of city facilities.
choices.b: No, because this organization is not a state actor and, therefore, its activities are not subject to the provisions of the Fourteenth Amendment.
choices.c: Yes, because the Fourteenth Amendment prohibits such an organization from discriminating against women in any of its activities to which it has invited members of the general public.
choices.d: Yes, because the organization's use of the city auditorium for this purpose subjects its conduct to the provisions of the Fourteenth Amendment.

一个城市拥有并经营一个大型公共礼堂。该市将礼堂出租给任何希望用其举办会议、讲座、音乐会或比赛的团体。每个使用者必须支付损坏押金并支付租金，租金仅按承租人实际使用建筑物的时间计算。预订遵循先到先得的原则。

一个只允许男性担任其最高职位的私人组织租用了该礼堂以举办其全国代表大会。该组织计划在大会上任命其新任官员。该组织广泛宣传了此次活动，邀请公众参加在市立礼堂举行的任命仪式。没有任何法规或行政规定禁止该组织将其最高职位限制于男性。

一位适当的原告起诉该私人组织，寻求禁止令，以阻止其使用市立礼堂举行新任官员的任命仪式。原告的唯一主张是，该组织使用此礼堂举行任命仪式违反了 Fourteenth Amendment，因为该组织取消了女性担任其最高职位的资格。

原告会胜诉吗？
options:
A. No, because the freedom of association protected by the Fourteenth Amendment prohibits the city from interfering in any way with the organization's use of city facilities.
不会，因为 Fourteenth Amendment 所保护的结社自由禁止市政府以任何方式干涉该组织对城市设施的使用。

B. No, because this organization is not a state actor and, therefore, its activities are not subject to the provisions of the Fourteenth Amendment.
不会，因为该组织不是一个州行为体（state actor），因此其活动不受 Fourteenth Amendment 条款的约束。

C. Yes, because the Fourteenth Amendment prohibits such an organization from discriminating against women in any of its activities to which it has invited members of the general public.
会，因为 Fourteenth Amendment 禁止此类组织在任何已邀请公众参加的活动中歧视女性。

D. Yes, because the organization's use of the city auditorium for this purpose subjects its conduct to the provisions of the Fourteenth Amendment.
会，因为该组织为此目的使用市立礼堂使其行为受到 Fourteenth Amendment 条款的约束。
data.explanation:
The Constitution (except the Thirteenth Amendment) applies to government actors. But under the state-action doctrine, a private actor is treated as a government actor - and similarly bound by the Constitution - when (1) the private actor performs a traditional and exclusive government function or (2) the government is significantly involved in the private actor's activities. Significant involvement exists when the government:
  • has a mutually beneficial relationship with the private actor (eg, joint venture)
  • creates a nexus by affirmatively facilitating or authorizing private action (eg, through a police officer acting under color of law) or
  • is pervasively intertwined in the private actor's management or control.


Here, the private organization is not performing a traditional and exclusive government function because private groups have historically used city auditoriums for conventions (Choice D). And merely leasing the auditorium does not affirmatively facilitate the organization's actions or entwine the city in the organization's management. Nor does it create a mutually beneficial relationship since the city provides uniform access to any group at the same rate on a first-come, first-served basis. Therefore, the organization is not a state actor subject to the Fourteenth Amendment.

(Choice A) The First Amendment - applicable to states and municipalities through the Fourteenth Amendment - prohibits some (but not all) government interference with the freedom of association.

(Choice C) The fact that the private organization invited members of the general public to its activities does not make it a government actor subject to the Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause.

Educational objective: Under the state-action doctrine, private actors are considered government actors and bound by the Constitution when (1) they perform a traditional government function or (2) the government is significantly involved in their activities - eg, more than providing access to government services or facilities.



选项正确率统计：A选项 3%，B选项 88%（正确选项），C选项 1%，D选项 6%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

宪法（Thirteenth Amendment 除外）适用于政府行为体。但是，根据州行为学说 (state-action doctrine)，当 (1) 私人行为体履行传统且排他性的政府职能或 (2) 政府深度参与私人行为体的活动时，该私人行为体被视为政府行为体，并同样受到宪法的约束。深度参与存在于政府：
  • 与私人行为体有互利关系（例如，合资企业）
  • 通过主动促进或授权私人行为（例如，通过一名在法律授权下行事的警官）来建立联系 (nexus) 或
  • 与私人行为体的管理或控制普遍交织在一起。


在本案中，该私人组织并未履行传统且排他性的政府职能，因为私人团体历来都使用市立礼堂举办会议（选项 D）。并且，仅仅租赁礼堂并不构成主动促进该组织的行为，也未使市政府与该组织的管理交织在一起。这也没有建立互利关系，因为该市在先到先得的基础上，以相同的费率向任何团体提供统一的准入。因此，该组织并非受 Fourteenth Amendment 约束的州行为体。

（选项 A） First Amendment——通过 Fourteenth Amendment 适用于各州和市政当局——禁止政府对结社自由进行某些（但非全部）干涉。

（选项 C） 该私人组织邀请公众参加其活动这一事实，并不会使其成为受 Fourteenth Amendment 平等保护条款约束的政府行为体。

教学目标：根据州行为学说 (state-action doctrine)，当 (1) 私人行为体履行传统政府职能，或 (2) 政府深度参与其活动——例如，不仅仅是提供政府服务或设施的准入——时，该私人行为体被视为政府行为体并受宪法约束。

References

Gilmore v. Montgomery, 417 U.S. 556, 574 (1974) (explaining that the mere private use of government facilities does not constitute significant state involvement under the state-action doctrine).

MBE 考题解析

Constitutional Law: State Action
⚖️ 核心考点：州行为原则 (State Action Doctrine)

美国宪法第十四修正案 (14th Amendment) 仅限制政府行为，不限制私人行为。除非存在例外情况，私人组织的歧视行为并不违反宪法。

案情关键点分析
  • 主体：一个私人组织 (Private Organization)。
  • 行为：租用市政府拥有的礼堂举办活动，且该组织内部规定歧视女性。
  • 政府角色：市政府仅仅是房东，按“先到先得”原则出租，收取租金，没有参与组织的管理或决策。
为何选 B？

本题的关键在于判断该私人组织是否因为租用了公共设施而变成了“州行为体” (State Actor)。

根据最高法院的判例（如 Gilmore v. Montgomery），仅仅使用公共设施并不足以构成“州行为”。要将私人行为转化为州行为，通常需要满足以下两个条件之一：

  1. 公共职能例外 (Public Function Exception)：私人实体行使了传统上由政府独占的权力（如管理城镇、举行选举）。
    → 租礼堂开会显然不是政府独占的职能。
  2. 纠缠/参与例外 (Entanglement/Involvement Exception)：政府在很大程度上授权、鼓励或从私人歧视中获利（如 Burton v. Wilmington Parking Authority 中的共生关系）。
    → 本案中，市政府只是中立地出租场地，没有“深度参与” (Significant Involvement)。
正确
选项 B 指出该组织不是州行为体，因此不受第十四修正案约束。这是原告败诉的根本原因。
干扰项排除
选项 D
错误理由：仅仅“使用” (Use) 城市礼堂并不足以建立州行为。如果只要用了水电或走了公路就受宪法约束，那宪法将无限扩大。
选项 C
错误理由：“邀请公众” (Inviting the public) 并不使私人俱乐部变成政府。虽然民权法案 (Civil Rights Acts) 可能通过立法禁止公共场所歧视，但本题问的是宪法第十四修正案，而宪法本身不直接约束此类私人行为。
🎓 MBE 考试技巧

遇到“私人歧视”被起诉违反“宪法”的题目时，首先问自己：“这是政府在歧视吗？”

如果被告是私人： 1. 除非它是“公司市镇” (Company Town)； 2. 或者政府与它有“共生关系” (Symbiotic Relationship)（如利润分成）；
否则，宪法管不着它！直接选“No, because not a state actor”。

questions.question:
In an effort to prevent quid pro quo corruption between donors and candidates for state elective office, a state enacted a law that limits the total amount an individual may contribute to individual candidates during an election cycle. A donor who was fined for violating this statute has argued that it is unconstitutional.
Is the state law constitutional?

choices.a: No, because political speech cannot be restricted.
choices.b: No, because the law is not the least restrictive means to serve a compelling state interest.
choices.c: Yes, because campaign contributions are not speech protected by the First Amendment.
choices.d: Yes, because the law is closely drawn to serve an important state interest.

data.questionStem:
Q82096

In an effort to prevent quid pro quo corruption between donors and candidates for state elective office, a state enacted a law that limits the total amount an individual may contribute to individual candidates during an election cycle. A donor who was fined for violating this statute has argued that it is unconstitutional.

Is the state law constitutional?

为防止州民选公职的捐赠者与候选人之间发生交换条件式腐败，某州颁布了一项法律，限制个人在选举周期内可向个别候选人捐赠的总金额。一名因违反该法规而被罚款的捐赠者主张，该法规违宪。

该州法律是否合宪？
options:
A. No, because political speech cannot be restricted.
否，因为政治言论不能被限制。

B. No, because the law is not the least restrictive means to serve a compelling state interest.
否，因为该法律并非为达成一项迫切的州利益而采取的限制性最小的手段。

C. Yes, because campaign contributions are not speech protected by the First Amendment.
是，因为竞选捐款并非受First Amendment保护的言论。

D. Yes, because the law is closely drawn to serve an important state interest.
是，因为该法律是为服务于一项重要的州利益而紧密拟定的。
data.explanation:
Campaign-finance restrictions


Contribution
restrictions		Limit on amount of contribution to:
  • single candidate
  • political candidates, parties & action committees combined
  • Increase of limit on amount of contribution to candidate when self-financed opponent exceeds certain spending amount
Intermediate scrutiny
closely drawn/substantially related to important government interest
Expenditure
restrictions		Limit on spending by:
  • corporations or unions in support of or opposition to candidate
  • candidate on his/her own behalf
Strict scrutiny
necessary/least restrictive means to achieve compelling government interest
The First Amendment protects political speech, which includes campaign contributions and expenditures (Choice C). Political speech is fundamental to a free and democratic society but may be restricted if the government satisfies the appropriate level of scrutiny (Choice A). A government restriction on campaign contributions must survive intermediate scrutiny , which requires the government to prove that its restriction is closely drawn to serve (ie, substantially related to) an important government interest.

Here, the state law limits the amount that an individual may contribute to a single candidate for state elective office during an election cycle. The state has an important interest in preventing quid pro quo corruption between donors and candidates.† And in Buckley v. Valeo , the U.S. Supreme Court held that limiting the amount of money an individual may donate to a single candidate is closely drawn to serve that interest. Therefore, the state law is constitutional.

†Preventing quid pro quo corruption or the appearance of it is the only government interest that the U.S. Supreme Court has recognized is important enough to justify government restrictions on campaign contributions.

(Choice B) A government restriction on campaign expenditures must satisfy strict scrutiny - ie, the government must show that its restriction is the least restrictive means to serve a compelling government interest. However, this law restricts campaign contributions , so the state need only satisfy intermediate scrutiny.

Educational objective: The First Amendment protects political speech, which includes campaign contributions and expenditures. A law that restricts campaign contributions is unconstitutional unless the government satisfies intermediate scrutiny by showing that the law is closely drawn to serve (ie, substantially related to) an important government interest.

选项正确率统计：A选项 5%，B选项 29%，C选项 14%，D选项 50%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

竞选财务限制


捐款
限制		对以下项目的捐款金额限制：
  • 单一候选人
  • 政治候选人、政党及政治行动委员会的合计
  • 当自筹资金的对手超过特定支出金额时，提高对候选人的捐款金额上限
中度审查
为重要政府利益而紧密拟定/与之实质相关
支出
限制		对以下对象的支出限制：
  • 支持或反对候选人的公司或工会
  • 候选人代表其本人
严格审查
为实现迫切政府利益所必需的/限制性最小的手段
First Amendment 保护政治言论，其中包括竞选捐款和支出(选项 C)。政治言论是自由民主社会的基石，但如果政府满足适当级别的审查，则可能受到限制(选项 A)。政府对竞选捐款的限制必须经受中度审查，这要求政府证明其限制是为服务于（即，实质上关系到）一项重要的政府利益而紧密拟定的。

在本案中，该州法律限制了个人在选举周期内可向单一州民选公职候选人捐款的数额。该州在防止捐赠者与候选人之间的交换条件式腐败方面拥有重要的利益。† 并且，在 Buckley v. Valeo 案中，美国最高法院裁定，限制个人可向单一候选人捐赠的金额是为服务于该利益而紧密拟定的。因此，该州法律是合宪的。

†防止交换条件式腐败或其表象，是美国最高法院承认的唯一足以证明政府对竞选捐款进行限制是正当的政府利益。

(选项 B) 政府对竞选支出的限制必须满足严格审查——即，政府必须表明其限制是为达成一项迫切的政府利益而采取的限制性最小的手段。然而，本法限制的是竞选捐款，因此该州仅需满足中度审查。

教学目的：First Amendment 保护政治言论，其中包括竞选捐款和支出。一项限制竞选捐款的法律是违宪的，除非政府能通过证明该法律是为服务于（即，实质上关系到）一项重要的政府利益而紧密拟定的，从而满足中度审查。

References

Buckley v. Valeo, 424 U.S. 1, 29 (1976) (holding that a limit on the amount an individual may donate to a candidate is a constitutional means to serve the government's important interest in combating quid pro quo corruption).

MBE 考点解析

宪法：竞选资金与言论自由

✅ 正确答案：D

是的，因为该法律是为服务于一项重要的州利益而紧密拟定的 (Closely drawn to serve an important state interest)。

⚖️ 核心法律规则

本题的核心在于区分竞选捐款 (Campaign Contributions) 和 竞选支出 (Campaign Expenditures) 的审查标准。

根据美国最高法院在 Buckley v. Valeo (1976) 中的裁定：

类型 审查标准 (Scrutiny) 合宪性
捐款限制
(Contributions)		 中度审查 / 紧密拟定
(Intermediate / Closely Drawn)		 通常合宪
(如果为了防止腐败)
支出限制
(Expenditures)		 严格审查
(Strict Scrutiny)		 通常违宪
(很难满足标准)
🔍 深度解析

1. 为什么是“紧密拟定” (Closely Drawn)？

法院认为，限制一个人给候选人捐多少钱，对言论自由的限制相对较小（只是限制了表达支持的“音量”，而不是禁止表达支持本身）。因此，政府不需要证明这是“限制最小的手段” (Least restrictive means)，只需要证明该法律与重要的政府利益 (Important government interest) 密切相关。

2. 什么是“重要的政府利益”？

在本案中，防止“交换条件式腐败” (Quid pro quo corruption) 或其表象，被法院认定为足够重要的利益，可以正当化对捐款的限制。

3. 结合题目：

题目中该州法律限制的是“个人捐赠的总金额” (Contribution)。因此，适用中度审查（Closely Drawn）。选项 D 准确地复述了这一法律标准。

❌ 为什么其他选项错误？

选项 A 错误： 虽然政治言论受保护，但它不是绝对的。为了防止腐败，政府可以进行适当限制。

选项 B 错误： 这是一个典型的陷阱选项。它描述的是严格审查 (Strict Scrutiny) 的标准（"least restrictive means" + "compelling interest"）。严格审查适用于限制候选人花多少钱（支出），而不适用于限制捐赠者给多少钱（捐款）。

选项 C 错误： 竞选捐款确实属于受第一修正案保护的言论形式（Money is speech），只是受保护程度不如直接的政治演说高，因此可以受到更严格的监管，但不能说它完全不受保护。

💡 MBE 考试技巧

在遇到竞选资金 (Campaign Finance) 的题目时，第一步先判断限制的对象：

  • 如果是限制给钱 (Giving/Contribution) ➡️ 标准较低 ➡️ 法律通常有效。
  • 如果是限制花钱 (Spending/Expenditure) ➡️ 标准极高 ➡️ 法律通常无效。

记住口诀："You can limit the giving, but you can't limit the spending."

questions.question:
A state statute prohibits any retailer of books, magazines, pictures, or posters from "publicly displaying or selling to any person any material that may be harmful to minors because of the violent or sexually explicit nature of its pictorial content." Violation of this statute is a misdemeanor.
A corner store displays publicly and sells magazines containing violent and sexually explicit pictures. The owner of this store is prosecuted under the above statute for these actions.
In defending against this prosecution in a state trial court, which of the following is the best defense for the corner store?

choices.a: Equal protection of the laws, because the statute irrationally distinguishes between violent and sexually explicit pictorial material that may harm minors and such material that may harm only adults.
choices.b: Equal protection of the laws, because the statute irrationally treats violent and sexually explicit material that is pictorial differently from such material that is composed wholly of printed words.
choices.c: First Amendment as it is incorporated into the Fourteenth Amendment, because a state may not prohibit the sale of violent or sexually explicit material in the absence of proof that the material is utterly without any redeeming value in the marketplace of ideas.
choices.d: First Amendment as it is incorporated into the Fourteenth Amendment, because the statute is excessively vague and overbroad.

data.questionStem:
Q82099

A state statute prohibits any retailer of books, magazines, pictures, or posters from "publicly displaying or selling to any person any material that may be harmful to minors because of the violent or sexually explicit nature of its pictorial content." Violation of this statute is a misdemeanor.

A corner store displays publicly and sells magazines containing violent and sexually explicit pictures. The owner of this store is prosecuted under the above statute for these actions.

In defending against this prosecution in a state trial court, which of the following is the best defense for the corner store?

某州法规禁止任何书籍、杂志、图片或海报的零售商“向任何人公开展示或销售任何因其图像内容的暴力或色情性质而可能对未成年人有害的材料”。违反本法规属轻罪。

一家街角商店公开展示并销售含有暴力和色情图片的杂志。该店主因这些行为根据上述法规被起诉。

在州初审法院为此案进行辩护时，以下哪项是该街角商店的最佳辩护理由？
options:
A. Equal protection of the laws, because the statute irrationally distinguishes between violent and sexually explicit pictorial material that may harm minors and such material that may harm only adults.
法律的平等保护，因为该法规不合理地区分了可能损害未成年人的暴力和色情图像材料，以及仅可能损害成年人的此类材料。

B. Equal protection of the laws, because the statute irrationally treats violent and sexually explicit material that is pictorial differently from such material that is composed wholly of printed words.
法律的平等保护，因为该法规不合理地将图像形式的暴力和色情材料与完全由印刷文字组成的此类材料区别对待。

C. First Amendment as it is incorporated into the Fourteenth Amendment, because a state may not prohibit the sale of violent or sexually explicit material in the absence of proof that the material is utterly without any redeeming value in the marketplace of ideas.
经由第十四修正案合并适用于各州的宪法第一修正案，因为在没有证据证明材料在思想市场上完全没有任何可取价值的情况下，一个州不得禁止销售暴力或色情材料。

D. First Amendment as it is incorporated into the Fourteenth Amendment, because the statute is excessively vague and overbroad.
经由第十四修正案合并适用于各州的宪法第一修正案，因为该法规过度模糊和过分宽泛。
data.explanation:
The First Amendment free speech clause (applied to the states through the Fourteenth Amendment ) protects the free flow of ideas with limited exceptions. A law that infringes upon this right can be challenged on its face and struck down in its entirety under either:
  • the overbreadth doctrine - renders laws unconstitutional if they restrict a substantial amount of protected speech or
  • the vagueness doctrine - renders laws unconstitutional if ordinary persons would have to guess the law's meaning because the law fails to provide notice of what speech is prohibited.
Here, the state statute regulates speech by prohibiting retailers from publicly displaying or selling any material containing violent or sexually explicit pictures that may be harmful to minors. Although some violent or sexually explicit speech is not protected by the First Amendment, a substantial amount is. Therefore, the overbreadth doctrine is a defense against the enforcement of this statute. And since this statute also requires ordinary persons to guess as to which materials may be harmful to minors, the vagueness doctrine is another valid defense.

(Choices A & B) The Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause prohibits states from treating similarly situated persons (or classes of persons) differently without adequate justification. But here, there is no evidence that this law is being applied in a discriminatory manner - eg, had corner store owners, but no other retailers, been prosecuted under the statute. Therefore, an equal protection defense would likely fail.

(Choice C) A state may prohibit the sale of violent or sexually explicit material if (1) it falls outside of the First Amendment's protections - eg, material that incites crime or is obscene under the Miller test - or (2) this content-based restriction passes strict scrutiny. Neither requires proof that the material is utterly without any redeeming value in the marketplace of ideas.

Educational objective: A law that interferes with the freedom of speech will be struck down on its face if it restricts a substantial amount of protected speech (ie, overbroad) OR fails to give ordinary persons notice of the prohibited speech (ie, unduly vague).



选项正确率统计：A选项 1%，B选项 1%，C选项 24%，D选项 72%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

宪法第一修正案的言论自由条款（通过第十四修正案适用于各州）保护思想的自由流动，但有有限的例外。一项侵犯此项权利的法律可因其本身内容而受到质疑，并可基于以下任一原则被完全推翻：
  • 过度宽泛原则 (overbreadth doctrine) - 如果法律限制了大量的受保护言论，则该法律违宪；或
  • 模糊原则 (vagueness doctrine) - 如果法律未能告知何种言论被禁止，以致普通人必须猜测其含义，则该法律违宪。
在此案中，州法规通过禁止零售商公开展示或销售任何含有可能对未成年人有害的暴力或色情图片的材料来监管言论。尽管某些暴力或色情言论不受第一修正案的保护，但有相当一部分是受保护的。因此，过度宽泛原则是反对执行该法规的一项辩护理由。并且，由于该法规还要求普通人猜测哪些材料可能对未成年人有害，因此模糊原则是另一项有效的辩护理由。

(选项 A 和 B) 第十四修正案的平等保护条款禁止各州在没有充分理由的情况下，区别对待处境相似的个人（或群体）。但在此案中，没有证据表明该法律的适用存在歧视性——例如，只有街角商店的店主，而没有其他零售商，根据该法规被起诉。因此，基于平等保护的辩护很可能会失败。

(选项 C) 一个州可以禁止销售暴力或色情材料，如果 (1) 它不属于第一修正案的保护范围——例如，煽动犯罪的材料或根据 Miller 测试被认定为淫秽的材料——或 (2) 这种基于内容的限制通过了严格审查。这两者都不要求证明该材料在思想市场上完全没有任何可取价值。

教学目标：一项干涉言论自由的法律，如果它限制了大量的受保护言论（即，过度宽泛）或未能向普通人告知被禁止的言论（即，过度模糊），则将因其本身内容而被推翻。

References

Watchtower Bible & Tract Soc'y of N.Y., Inc. v. Vill. of Stratton, 536 U.S. 150, 165 (2002) (finding an ordinance overbroad since it prohibits all door-to-door, not just commercial, canvassing without a license).

Gentile v. State Bar of Nev., 501 U.S. 1030, 1057 - 58 (1991) (striking down a law for vagueness since it tends to mislead attorneys about potential punishment for pretrial publicity of clients' criminal defenses).

MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: First Amendment
最佳辩护理由 (Best Defense) 选项 D： 经由第十四修正案合并适用于各州的宪法第一修正案，因为该法规过度模糊和过分宽泛 (Vague and Overbroad)。

本题考查的是对言论自由限制的表面违宪审查 (Facial Challenge)。当法规涉及言论自由时，如果其措辞不当，即使被告的行为本身可能不受保护，被告仍可主张该法规整体违宪。

1. 过度宽泛 (Overbreadth)

定义：如果一项法律在禁止不受保护的言论（如淫秽内容）的同时，也禁止了大量的受保护言论，则该法律是“过度宽泛”的。

本案分析：

  • 法规禁止向任何人 (any person) 销售可能对未成年人有害的材料。
  • 这意味着成年人也无法购买这些材料。
  • 关键判例：在 Butler v. Michigan (1957) 中，最高法院指出，州政府不能为了保护未成年人，而将成年人的阅读范围限制在适合儿童的水平（"burn the house to roast the pig"）。
  • 因此，该法规侵犯了成年人获取受第一修正案保护的非淫秽材料的权利。
2. 模糊性 (Vagueness)

定义：根据正当程序条款 (Due Process Clause)，如果法律未能给普通人提供关于何种行为被禁止的合理通知 (Reasonable Notice)，则该法律无效。

本案分析：

  • 法规使用了“可能对未成年人有害 (may be harmful to minors)”这一表述。
  • 如果没有具体的定义或标准（如具体的年龄分级或明确的淫秽定义），店主必须去猜测什么内容是违法的。
  • 这种不确定性会产生寒蝉效应 (Chilling Effect)，导致人们为了避免受罚而不敢行使合法的言论自由权利。
为什么其他选项是错的？
🚫 选项 A & B (Equal Protection)：

虽然平等保护条款禁止不合理的分类，但在言论自由案件中，如果法律直接限制了言论内容，法院首选的分析工具是第一修正案，而不是平等保护。此外，区分“文字与图片”或“成人与儿童的伤害”通常能通过合理性审查 (Rational Basis)，但这并不能解决其侵犯言论自由的核心问题。

🚫 选项 C (Redeeming Value)：

这个选项引用了一个过时的标准。现在的淫秽定义来自 Miller v. California，要求材料缺乏“严肃的文学、艺术、政治或科学价值”。法律不需要证明材料“完全没有任何 (utterly without any)”价值就能禁止它。只要符合 Miller 标准，州政府就可以监管。

🎓 MBE 考试技巧：

当你看到题目中的法规原文包含广泛的禁止性语言（如 "any material", "any person"）且涉及言论内容时，首先要考虑Overbreadth（过度宽泛）和Vagueness（模糊性）。

如果法规为了保护儿童而限制了成年人的访问权，这几乎总是违反第一修正案的。

questions.question:
A doctor who was licensed to practice medicine in a particular state was convicted in state court of improperly distributing specified drugs by writing prescriptions for fictitious persons. Under state law, such an abuse of the prescription-writing privilege requires revocation of a doctor's license. After it received an official notification of the doctor's conviction, the state medical board revoked the doctor's license without affording him any opportunity for a hearing.
The doctor has sued the board in state court to set aside the revocation, alleging deprivation of property without due process of law because the board did not provide an opportunity for a trial-type hearing before revoking the license. The doctor does not deny the conviction or the factual basis for it.
Which of the following is the strongest argument in support of the state medical board?

choices.a: A doctor's license to practice is a privilege, not a right, and therefore is not property within the meaning of the due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.
choices.b: Due process requires a balancing of interests, and the state's interest in preventing drug abuse outweighs the doctor's interest in the particular procedure followed in the disciplinary proceeding.
choices.c: The adjudicative facts necessary to revoke the doctor's license were determined in the criminal trial, and therefore due process does not require any further trial-type hearing.
choices.d: The licensing board was required to summarily revoke the doctor's license because Article IV, Section 1, of the Constitution requires the licensing board to give full faith and credit to the doctor's criminal conviction.

data.questionStem:
Q82817 A doctor who was licensed to practice medicine in a particular state was convicted in state court of improperly distributing specified drugs by writing prescriptions for fictitious persons. Under state law, such an abuse of the prescription-writing privilege requires revocation of a doctor's license. After it received an official notification of the doctor's conviction, the state medical board revoked the doctor's license without affording him any opportunity for a hearing.

The doctor has sued the board in state court to set aside the revocation, alleging deprivation of property without due process of law because the board did not provide an opportunity for a trial-type hearing before revoking the license. The doctor does not deny the conviction or the factual basis for it.

Which of the following is the strongest argument in support of the state medical board? 一名在某州获得行医执照的医生，因给虚构人物开具处方，不当分发特定药物而被州法院定罪。根据州法律，滥用处方权的此种行为需要吊销医生的执照。州医疗委员会在收到该医生被定罪的正式通知后，未经听证程序即吊销了该医生的执照。

该医生已向州法院起诉该委员会，要求撤销吊销决定，声称委员会在吊销其执照前未提供审判式听证的机会，侵犯了其未经正当法律程序而被剥夺财产的权利。该医生并未否认其定罪或其事实依据。

以下哪项是支持州医疗委员会的最有力论点？
options:
A. A doctor's license to practice is a privilege, not a right, and therefore is not property within the meaning of the due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.
医生的行医执照是一种特权，而非权利，因此不属于《第十四修正案》正当程序条款所指的财产。

B. Due process requires a balancing of interests, and the state's interest in preventing drug abuse outweighs the doctor's interest in the particular procedure followed in the disciplinary proceeding.
正当程序要求利益衡量，而州在防止药物滥用方面的利益，重于医生在纪律处分程序中所遵循的特定程序中的利益。

C. The adjudicative facts necessary to revoke the doctor's license were determined in the criminal trial, and therefore due process does not require any further trial-type hearing.
吊销医生执照所需的裁决性事实已在刑事审判中确定，因此正当程序不要求任何进一步的审判式听证。

D. The licensing board was required to summarily revoke the doctor's license because Article IV, Section 1, of the Constitution requires the licensing board to give full faith and credit to the doctor's criminal conviction.
执照委员会被要求立即吊销医生的执照，因为《宪法》第四条第一款要求执照委员会对医生的刑事定罪给予充分信任和尊重。
data.explanation:
Procedural due process requires the government to provide notice and a meaningful opportunity to be heard before depriving a person of life, liberty, or property. The specific procedures required are determined by the Mathews v. Eldridge three-factor balancing test:

  1. The private interest affected. Here, the doctor's interest in his professional license and livelihood is a very significant property interest.
  2. The risk of an erroneous deprivation through the procedures used, and the probable value of additional safeguards. This is the key factor in this case. The risk of error is virtually zero because the dispositive fact—the illegal distribution of drugs—was already established in a full criminal trial with the highest procedural protections (e.g., proof beyond a reasonable doubt). A second, duplicative hearing before the board would have negligible value.
  3. The government's interest. This interest is primarily about the fiscal and administrative burdens that additional procedures would entail. Forcing the state to conduct a full, trial-type hearing when the facts have already been conclusively litigated would be inefficient and costly, burdening the government with no corresponding benefit in accuracy.
Given this balance, particularly the extremely low value of an additional hearing (Factor 2) and the high burden it would impose (Factor 3), no further trial-type hearing is required by due process. Therefore, the board's strongest argument is that the necessary facts were already determined in the criminal proceeding.

(Choice A) This is incorrect. The outdated distinction between "rights" and "privileges" has been abandoned. A professional license is a protected property interest.

(Choice B) This choice is incorrect because it is a deliberate and sophisticated misstatement of the Mathews test, designed to trap test-takers who have a vague memory of a "balancing test." It creates a false comparison between the government's broad substantive goal ("interest in preventing drug abuse") and the individual's narrow procedural interest ("interest in the particular procedure"). The actual Mathews test, as outlined above, is a structured procedural analysis that balances the private property interest itself (the license), the risk of error, and the government's burden. Choice B distorts this framework by creating an improper and simplistic balancing act that omits the crucial analysis of procedural risk and value.

(Choice D) The Full Faith and Credit Clause applies to recognizing judgments from other states and is therefore inapplicable here.



程序性正当程序要求政府在剥夺个人的生命、自由或财产前，提供通知和有意义的被听证机会。具体需要何种程序，由著名的《Mathews v. Eldridge》案三要素衡量测试决定：

  1. 受影响的私人利益。 在此案中，医生在其职业执照和生计中的利益是一项非常重大的财产利益。
  2. 通过现有程序导致错误剥夺的风险，以及额外程序保障的可能价值。 这是本案的关键因素。发生错误的风险几乎为零，因为决定性的事实——非法分发药物——已经在一次完整的刑事审判中被确立，该审判拥有最高级别的程序保护（例如，排除合理怀疑的证明标准）。在医疗委员会面前就完全相同的事实举行第二次、重复性的听证，其价值可以忽略不计。
  3. 政府的利益。 这项利益主要关乎额外程序将带来的财政和行政负担。当事实已经被最终诉讼确定后，强迫州政府再进行一次完整的审判式听证将是低效且昂贵的，这给政府增加了负担，却在准确性上带不来任何相应的好处。
综合此番衡量，特别是考虑到额外听证的价值极低（第二要素）及其将施加的沉重负担（第三要素），正当程序不要求任何进一步的审判式听证。因此，委员会最强有力的论点是，必要的事实已在刑事诉讼中确定。

（选项 A） 这是不正确的。“权利”与“特权”的过时区分已被摒弃。职业执照是一项受保护的财产利益。

（选项 B） 这个选项是错误的，因为它是一个经过精心设计的、对Mathews测试的故意歪曲，旨在诱捕那些只对“利益衡量测试”有模糊记忆的考生。它在政府宽泛的实体目标（“防止药物滥用的利益”）和个人狭隘的程序利益（“在特定程序中的利益”）之间创造了一个错误的比较。如上所述，实际的Mathews测试是一个结构化的程序分析，它衡量的是私人财产利益本身（执照）、出错的风险以及政府的负担。选项B通过构建一个不恰当且过于简单的权衡，忽略了对程序风险和价值的关键分析，从而扭曲了整个框架。

（选项 D） “充分信任和尊重条款”适用于承认其他州的判决，因此在本案中不适用。

References

  • Mathews v. Eldridge, 424 U.S. 319, 335 (1976) (listing the three factors used to assess compliance with procedural due process).

MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Procedural Due Process
⚖️ 核心考点：Mathews v. Eldridge 测试

在决定政府剥夺个人财产（如执照）前需要何种程序时，法院使用三要素平衡测试：

  1. 私人利益 (Private Interest)：被剥夺权益的重要性。
  2. 错误风险 (Risk of Error)：现有程序的出错概率及额外程序的价值。
  3. 政府利益 (Government Interest)：行政效率和财政负担。

✅ 为什么选 C？

正确答案 裁决性事实已在刑事审判中确定

本题的关键在于 Mathews 测试的第二个要素：额外程序的价值。

医生已经被刑事法庭定罪。刑事审判的证明标准是“排除合理怀疑” (Beyond a reasonable doubt)，这是最高的证明标准。既然事实已经在刑事法庭上被严格证实，那么在行政听证会上再次确认这些事实（通常仅需“优势证据”标准）是毫无必要的重复。

因此，在此情境下，举行听证会来确认“医生是否开了假处方”这一事实，其错误剥夺的风险几乎为零，额外听证会的价值也为零。

❌ 为什么其他选项错误？

高频陷阱 选项 B：利益衡量 (Balancing of Interests)

这是一个精心设计的干扰项。虽然正当程序确实涉及“利益衡量”，但选项 B 的表述是错误的。

它错误地将“政府防止药物滥用的宏观利益”与“医生对特定程序的微观利益”进行对比。真正的 Mathews 测试衡量的是：增加额外程序的行政负担 vs. 该程序减少错误判决的价值。选项 B 忽略了本案中“事实已被刑事定罪确认”这一核心逻辑。

错误观念 选项 A：权利 vs. 特权 (Right vs. Privilege)

这是一个过时的法律概念。现代宪法学（自 Goldberg v. Kelly 等案以来）已经废弃了“权利与特权”的区别。职业执照被视为受第十四修正案保护的财产利益 (Property Interest)。

适用错误 选项 D：充分信任和尊重 (Full Faith and Credit)

该条款 (Article IV, Section 1) 主要适用于州与州之间承认判决。本案是同一个州内部的刑事法院和行政机构之间的关系，因此该条款不适用。

💡 MBE 解题技巧：
当题目涉及“基于刑事定罪的行政处罚”时，通常不需要新的事实听证会。因为刑事定罪提供了最高级别的程序保护，这本身就满足了 Due Process 对事实认定的要求。

questions.question:
A purchaser bought land in the mountain foothills just outside a resort town and planned to build a housing development there. Soon thereafter, the county in which the land was located unexpectedly adopted a regulation that, for the first time, prohibited all construction in several foothill and mountain areas, including the area of the purchaser's property. The purpose of the county's regulation was "to conserve for future generations the unique natural wildlife and plant habitats" in the mountain areas. Since the adoption of the regulation, the purchaser has been unable to lease or sell the property at any price. Several realtors have advised the purchaser that his property is now worthless.
The purchaser has sued the county, claiming that the regulation has effected a taking of the purchaser's property and that the county therefore owes the purchaser just compensation.
Is the court likely to rule in favor of the purchaser?

choices.a: No, because the county did not take title to the property from the purchaser.
choices.b: No, because the regulation has not caused or authorized any uninvited physical invasion or intrusion onto the property.
choices.c: Yes, because the conservation objective of the county ordinance is not sufficiently compelling to justify the substantial diminution in the property value.
choices.d: Yes, because the effect of the county's regulation is to deny the purchaser's investment-backed expectation and essentially all economically beneficial use of the property.

data.questionStem:
Q82106

A purchaser bought land in the mountain foothills just outside a resort town and planned to build a housing development there. Soon thereafter, the county in which the land was located unexpectedly adopted a regulation that, for the first time, prohibited all construction in several foothill and mountain areas, including the area of the purchaser's property. The purpose of the county's regulation was "to conserve for future generations the unique natural wildlife and plant habitats" in the mountain areas. Since the adoption of the regulation, the purchaser has been unable to lease or sell the property at any price. Several realtors have advised the purchaser that his property is now worthless.

The purchaser has sued the county, claiming that the regulation has effected a taking of the purchaser's property and that the county therefore owes the purchaser just compensation.

Is the court likely to rule in favor of the purchaser?

一名购买者在一个度假小镇外的山麓地带购买了土地，并计划在那里建造一个住宅开发项目。此后不久，该土地所在的县出人意料地通过了一项法规，首次禁止在包括购买者财产所在区域在内的几个山麓和山区进行所有建设。该县法规的目的是“为后代保护山区独特的自然野生动植物栖息地”。自该法规通过以来，购买者一直无法以任何价格出租或出售该房产。几位房地产经纪人已告知购买者，他的财产现在一文不值。

购买者已起诉该县，声称该法规构成了对其财产的征收，因此该县应向购买者支付公正补偿。

法院是否可能作出有利于购买者的裁决？
options:
A. No, because the county did not take title to the property from the purchaser.
不会，因为该县并未从购买者手中取得该财产的所有权。

B. No, because the regulation has not caused or authorized any uninvited physical invasion or intrusion onto the property.
不会，因为该法规并未导致或授权任何未经邀请的对该财产的物理侵占或侵入。

C. Yes, because the conservation objective of the county ordinance is not sufficiently compelling to justify the substantial diminution in the property value.
会，因为该县法令的保护目标不足以成为财产价值大幅减损的正当理由。

D. Yes, because the effect of the county's regulation is to deny the purchaser's investment-backed expectation and essentially all economically beneficial use of the property.
会，因为该县法规的效果是剥夺了购买者有投资支持的预期，以及该财产基本上所有的经济上有利的用途。
data.explanation:
Fifth Amendment takings


TypeAttributes
PhysicalPossession or permanent physical invasion of property
RegulatoryDeprivation of all economically beneficial uses Restricts use under totality of circumstances:
  • character of government action
  • economic impact
  • reasonable investment-back expectations
ExactionCondition to obtain building/development permit
A taking occurs when the government:
  • physically possesses or invades private property (ie, physical taking) or

  • deprives the owner of all economically beneficial use of the property but the owner retains possession (ie, regulatory taking) (Choices A & B).


And under the Fifth Amendment - as applied to the states through the Fourteenth Amendment - a taking must be for a public use, and the government must justly compensate the owner for the property's fair market value.

Here, the county's regulation prohibits all construction on the purchaser's land. This amounted to a regulatory taking because it denied the purchaser (1) his investment-backed expectation for the planned housing development and (2) essentially all economically beneficial use of the property. And since the property was rendered worthless, the court will likely rule that the purchaser is entitled to just compensation.

(Choice C) The ordinance's objective to conserve natural wildlife and plant habitats may be compelling. But the county can only justify the substantial diminution in the purchaser's property value by providing him just compensation.

Educational objective: A Fifth Amendment taking occurs when:
  • the government physically possesses or invades private property or
  • the owner retains possession but loses all economically beneficial use of the property due to government action.


选项正确率统计：A选项 4%，B选项 4%，C选项 3%，D选项 86%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

第五修正案的征收


类型特征
物理性占有或对财产的永久性物理侵占
管制性剥夺所有经济上有利的用途，在总体情况的考量下限制使用：
  • 政府行为的性质
  • 经济影响
  • 合理的有投资支持的预期
征地费为获得建筑/开发许可而设定的条件
当政府出现以下情况时，即构成征收：
  • 物理上占有或侵占私有财产（即物理性征收）或

  • 剥夺了所有者对财产的所有经济上有利的用途，但所有者保留占有权（即管制性征收）（选项 A & B）。


根据第五修正案——通过第十四修正案适用于各州——征收必须是为了公共用途，且政府必须就财产的公平市场价值向所有者提供公正补偿。

在本案中，该县的法规禁止在购买者的土地上进行任何建设。这构成了一次管制性征收，因为它剥夺了购买者（1）其对计划中的住宅开发项目的有投资支持的预期，以及（2）该财产基本上所有的经济上有利的用途。并且由于该财产已变得一文不值，法院很可能会裁定购买者有权获得公正补偿。

（选项 C） 该法令保护自然野生动植物栖息地的目标可能具有说服力。但该县只有通过向购买者提供公正补偿，才能为其财产价值的巨额减损提供正当理由。

教学目标：第五修正案的征收发生在以下情况：
  • 政府物理上占有或侵占私有财产，或
  • 所有者保留占有权，但因政府行为而丧失了财产所有经济上有利的用途。


References

Lucas v. S.C. Coastal Council, 505 U.S. 1003, 1019 (1992) (holding that a deprivation of all economically beneficial uses of property constitutes a taking).

26 Am Jur. 2d Eminent Domain § 12 (2019) (explaining a deprivation of all economically beneficial uses of property).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析：管制性征收
Regulatory Takings

本题考察的是美国宪法第五修正案（Fifth Amendment）中的征收条款（Takings Clause），特别是当政府法规导致财产价值完全丧失时的法律后果。

正确答案：D

深度解析

法院很可能会判决购买者胜诉，理由如下：

1. 管制性征收 (Regulatory Taking)
虽然政府没有物理上占有土地，但如果一项法规剥夺了所有者对该财产“所有经济上有利的用途” (all economically beneficial use)，这在法律上被视为一种“本身即构成征收” (per se taking)。

2. 事实认定
题目中明确指出：

  • 法规禁止了所有建设 (prohibited all construction)。
  • 该财产现在一文不值 (worthless)。
  • 购买者无法出售或租赁该土地。
这种程度的限制完全剥夺了购买者“有投资支持的预期” (investment-backed expectations)，即开发房产的计划。

3. 结论
根据第五修正案，当法规效果等同于完全剥夺财产价值时，政府必须支付公正补偿 (Just Compensation)，无论政府的初衷（如环境保护）多么高尚。

关键判例 (Key Precedent)

Lucas v. South Carolina Coastal Council (1992)

最高法院在该案中确立了规则：当一项法规剥夺了土地所有者100%的经济价值时，除非该限制源于普通法中的妨害（nuisance）原则，否则政府必须进行赔偿。这就是著名的“卢卡斯规则” (Lucas Rule)。

为什么其他选项是错的？

  • 选项 A 错误：征收不需要政府获得所有权 (title)。只要政府行为剥夺了财产的使用权或价值，即可构成征收。
  • 选项 B 错误：这混淆了物理性征收 (Physical Taking) 和管制性征收。虽然没有物理入侵，但法规限制本身已构成征收。
  • 选项 C 错误：这是一个常见的陷阱。虽然保护环境是合法的警察权 (Police Power) 行使，但这并不能免除政府在造成“完全经济价值丧失”时的赔偿责任。目的正当不代表可以免费剥夺私产。

MBE 备考锦囊

在处理 Takings Clause 问题时，请注意区分以下两种情况：
  1. 价值减少 (Diminution in Value)： 如果法规只是让土地贬值（例如减少了90%的价值但仍有剩余用途），通常应用 Penn Central 测试，法院不一定判为征收。
  2. 价值归零 (Total Deprivation)： 如果题目出现“worthless”（一文不值）或“denial of all economic use”（剥夺所有经济用途），这直接触发 Lucas 规则，几乎总是判定为征收并需要赔偿。

questions.question:
The Federal Family Film Enhancement Act assesses an excise tax of 10% on the price of admission to public movie theaters when they show films that contain actual or simulated scenes of human sexual intercourse.
Which of the following is the strongest argument against the constitutionality of this federal act?

choices.a: The act imposes a prior restraint on the freedom of speech protected by the First Amendment.
choices.b: The act imposes a tax solely on the basis of the content of speech without adequate justification and, therefore, it is prohibited by the freedom of speech clause of the First Amendment.
choices.c: The act is not rationally related to any legitimate national interest.
choices.d: The act violates the equal protection concepts embodied in the due process clause of the Fifth Amendment because it imposes a tax on the price of admission to view certain films and not on the price of admission to view comparable live performances.

data.questionStem:
Q82157

The Federal Family Film Enhancement Act assesses an excise tax of 10% on the price of admission to public movie theaters when they show films that contain actual or simulated scenes of human sexual intercourse.

Which of the following is the strongest argument against the constitutionality of this federal act?

《联邦家庭电影促进法案》（Federal Family Film Enhancement Act）规定，当公众电影院放映包含真实或模拟人类性交场景的电影时，需对其门票价格征收10%的消费税。

下列哪项是反对该联邦法案合宪性的最有力论点？
options:
A. The act imposes a prior restraint on the freedom of speech protected by the First Amendment.
该法案对受《第一修正案》保护的言论自由施加了事先限制。

B. The act imposes a tax solely on the basis of the content of speech without adequate justification and, therefore, it is prohibited by the freedom of speech clause of the First Amendment.
该法案仅基于言论内容征税，且无充分正当理由，因此，该行为被《第一修正案》的言论自由条款所禁止。

C. The act is not rationally related to any legitimate national interest.
该法案与任何合法的国家利益均不存在理性关联。

D. The act violates the equal protection concepts embodied in the due process clause of the Fifth Amendment because it imposes a tax on the price of admission to view certain films and not on the price of admission to view comparable live performances.
该法案违反了《第五修正案》正当程序条款所体现的平等保护理念，因为它对观看某些电影的门票价格征税，而对观看可比的现场表演的门票价格则不征税。
data.explanation:
Speech regulations


TypeDefinitionTest
Content-basedFacial discrimination Primary purpose targets message, subject, or ideaStrict scrutiny Necessary & narrowly tailored to achieve compelling interest
Content-neutralRegulates time, place, or manner of speechIntermediate scrutiny Narrowly tailored to achieve important interest Alternative avenues of communication remain
The First Amendment free speech clause protects the right to freely communicate and receive information and ideas. To ensure such protection, content-based restrictions on speech are presumptively unconstitutional and subject to strict scrutiny. This means that the government can only restrict speech based on what is being said (ie, its message or ideas) if it can prove that the restriction is necessary and narrowly tailored to achieve a compelling government interest - a nearly impossible task.

Here, the act is a content-based restriction on speech because it imposes an excise tax on the price of admission to theaters when they show films that depict human sexual intercourse. And since it is highly unlikely that this act can survive strict scrutiny, the strongest argument against its constitutionality is that it imposes a tax based solely on the content of speech without adequate justification.

(Choice A) A prior restraint on speech is a highly disfavored government action that prohibits speech before it even occurs (eg, injunction). But the act here is not a prior restraint on speech because it does not prevent the films from being shown - it merely imposes a tax.

(Choice C) If the federal act is not rationally related to a legitimate national interest, it cannot pass rational basis scrutiny - let alone strict scrutiny. But this argument would likely fail since laws almost always survive rational basis review.

(Choice D) This act may trigger the equal protection concepts embodied in the Fifth Amendment, which apply when the government treats similarly situated people differently. But since the movie theater patrons who must pay this tax are not part of a protected class, this is not a strong argument for challenging the act's validity.

Educational objective: Content-based restrictions on speech are unconstitutional unless they survive strict scrutiny. This incredibly stringent standard requires the government to prove that the restriction is necessary and narrowly tailored to achieve a compelling government interest.

选项正确率统计：A选项 8%，B选项 78%（正确选项），C选项 8%，D选项 4%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

言论规定


类型定义审查标准
基于内容的表面歧视
主要目的针对信息、主题或思想		严格审查
为实现迫切利益所必需且为狭义限定
内容中立的规定言论的时间、地点或方式中度审查
为实现重要利益而狭义限定
且保留其他沟通渠道
《第一修正案》的言论自由条款保护自由交流和接收信息与思想的权利。为确保此种保护，对言论的基于内容的限制被推定为违宪，并需接受严格审查。这意味着，政府只有在能够证明该限制是为实现迫切的政府利益所必需且为狭义限定的情况下，才能基于言论的内容（即其信息或思想）对言论进行限制——这几乎是一项不可能完成的任务。

在本案中，该法案是对言论的基于内容的限制，因为它对放映描绘人类性交场景电影的影院门票价格征收消费税。鉴于该法案极不可能通过严格审查，反对其合宪性的最有力论点是，它仅基于言论内容征税，且无充分正当理由。

(选项A) 对言论的事先限制是一种极不受欢迎的政府行为，它在言论发生前就予以禁止（例如，禁令）。但本案中的法案并非对言论的事先限制，因为它并未阻止电影的放映——它仅仅是征收了一项税款。

(选项C) 如果该联邦法案与合法的国家利益没有理性关联，它就无法通过理性基础审查——更不用说严格审查了。但这一论点很可能会失败，因为法律几乎总能通过理性基础审查。

(选项D) 该法案可能会触发《第五修正案》所体现的平等保护理念，该理念适用于政府对处境相似的人给予不同待遇的情况。但由于必须支付此项税款的电影院顾客不属于受保护阶层，因此这并非挑战该法案有效性的有力论据。

教学目标：对言论的基于内容的限制是违宪的，除非其能通过严格审查。这一极其严苛的标准要求政府证明，该限制是为实现迫切的政府利益所必需且为狭义限定的。

References

Ark. Writers' Project, Inc. v. Ragland, 481 U.S. 221, 231 (1987) (applying strict scrutiny to a tax scheme that exempts certain magazines based on content).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

宪法第一修正案与税收
核心原则：基于内容的规制 (Content-Based Regulation) 当政府对言论施加限制（包括税收）是基于言论的内容（即所表达的信息、主题或思想）时，该行为被推定为违宪，必须接受严格审查 (Strict Scrutiny)。
为何选项 B 是正确答案？

本题的核心在于识别该税收的性质。这项联邦税并非适用于所有电影票的通用销售税，而是专门针对包含特定内容（性交场景）的电影。

1. 识别歧视：
最高法院在 Arkansas Writers' Project, Inc. v. Ragland 等判例中确立，针对特定出版物或言论内容的差别税收（Differential Taxation）属于基于内容的规制。

2. 适用标准：
因为是基于内容的，政府必须证明该法律满足严格审查标准：

  • 必须为了实现迫切的政府利益 (Compelling Government Interest)。
  • 手段必须是狭义限定的 (Narrowly Tailored)。

3. 结论：
仅仅为了增加收入通常不足以构成“迫切利益”来正当化对言论内容的歧视。因此，最有力的论点是该法案基于内容征税且缺乏充分（迫切）的正当理由。

其他选项为何不够强？
选项 A 事先限制 (Prior Restraint)
虽然事先限制也是违宪的，但税收通常被视为事后的负担，而不是阻止言论发表的“禁令”或“许可制度”。除非税额高到构成事实上的禁止，否则法院更倾向于将其视为基于内容的惩罚，而非事先限制。
选项 C 理性基础 (Rational Basis)
这是一个陷阱。涉及言论自由的限制需要更高标准的审查（严格审查或中度审查），而不仅仅是“理性关联”。如果只用理性基础测试，政府很容易通过（例如声称为了保护家庭价值观），但这在第一修正案下是不够的。
选项 D 平等保护 (Equal Protection)
虽然差别待遇涉及平等保护，但在涉及基本权利（如言论自由）时，法院通常直接依据第一修正案进行分析。第一修正案的分析比第五修正案的平等保护分析更直接、更具体地针对言论内容歧视问题。
💡 MBE 考试技巧

看到政府对媒体、电影或出版物征税时，请立即检查：

  1. 通用税 (General Tax)：如果是对所有企业一视同仁的税，通常合宪。
  2. 特定税 (Specific Tax)：如果是专门针对媒体，或者针对特定内容的媒体征税，这就触发了严格审查。

本题中，“仅针对有性交场景的电影”就是明显的“基于内容”的信号。

Reference Case: Arkansas Writers' Project, Inc. v. Ragland, 481 U.S. 221 (1987).

questions.question:
Congress enacted a statute that made it illegal for "any employee, without the consent of his or her employer, to post on the Internet any information concerning the employer." The purpose of the statute was to prevent employees from revealing their employers' trade secrets.
Is the statute constitutional?

choices.a: No, because it is not narrowly tailored to further a compelling government interest.
choices.b: No, because it targets a particular medium of communication for special regulation.
choices.c: Yes, because it leaves open ample alternative channels of communication.
choices.d: Yes, because it prevents employees from engaging in unethical conduct.

Q82068

Congress enacted a statute that made it illegal for "any employee, without the consent of his or her employer, to post on the Internet any information concerning the employer." The purpose of the statute was to prevent employees from revealing their employers' trade secrets.

Is the statute constitutional?

国会颁布了一项法规，规定“任何雇员，未经其雇主同意，在互联网上发布任何有关其雇主的信息”均属非法。该法规的目的是防止雇员泄露其雇主的商业秘密。

该法规是否合宪？
options:
A. No, because it is not narrowly tailored to further a compelling government interest.
不合宪，因为它并非为促进某一重大的政府利益而经过严格限缩。

B. No, because it targets a particular medium of communication for special regulation.
不合宪，因为它针对某一特定的传播媒介进行特别管制。

C. Yes, because it leaves open ample alternative channels of communication.
合宪，因为它保留了充足的替代沟通渠道。

D. Yes, because it prevents employees from engaging in unethical conduct.
合宪，因为它阻止了雇员从事不道德的行为。
data.explanation:
The First Amendment free speech clause prohibits the government from unduly restricting an individual's right to freely communicate information and ideas. Restrictions based on the content of speech (ie, its message or ideas) are presumptively invalid and will only be upheld if they survive strict judicial scrutiny. Under this standard of review, the government has the nearly impossible task of proving that the restriction is necessary and narrowly tailored (ie, the least restrictive means) to further a compelling government interest.

Here, the statute targets speech based on its content since the statute prohibits employees from posting information concerning their employer. And though the government may have a compelling interest in preventing employees from revealing trade secrets, the statute is not necessary or narrowly tailored to further that interest. That is because less restrictive means could be used to protect trade secrets - eg, barring employees from posting information concerning their employers' trade secrets. As a result, the statute is unconstitutional.

(Choice B) A speech regulation does not violate the First Amendment simply because it targets a particular medium of communication (eg, Internet postings - as seen here).†

†In Packingham v. North Carolina, the Supreme Court equated the Internet to public streets and parks in dicta but never expressly held that the Internet is a public forum. Several cases dealing with this issue are currently being litigated in lower courts.

(Choice C) The availability of alternative channels of communication is one factor in evaluating content- neutral speech restrictions (ie, time, place, or manner restrictions). But since this statute is a content- based restriction, the fact that it leaves open channels of communication other than the Internet is irrelevant.

(Choice D) The statute may prevent employees from engaging in unethical conduct (eg, revealing trade secrets). But regardless, it is unconstitutional because it cannot survive strict scrutiny.

Educational objective: Content-based restrictions on speech are presumptively invalid and will only be upheld if they survive strict scrutiny - ie, the government must prove that the restriction is necessary and narrowly tailored to achieve a compelling government interest.



选项正确率统计：A选项 78%（正确选项），B选项 6%，C选项 12%，D选项 2%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

第一修正案 (First Amendment) 的言论自由条款禁止政府不当限制个人自由交流信息和思想的权利。基于言论内容（即其信息或思想）的限制被推定为无效，只有在通过严格司法审查时才能被维持。根据此审查标准，政府负有几乎不可能完成的证明责任，需证明该限制是为促进某一重大的政府利益所必需且经过严格限缩的（即限制最少的方式）。

在本案中，该法规是基于言论内容进行规制，因为它禁止雇员发布有关其雇主的信息。尽管政府在防止雇员泄露商业秘密方面可能拥有重大的利益，但该法规并非为促进该利益所必需或经过严格限缩的。这是因为可以采用限制性较小的方式来保护商业秘密——例如，仅禁止雇员发布有关其雇主商业秘密的信息。因此，该法规是违宪的。

（选项 B）一项言论规定并不会仅仅因为它针对某一特定的传播媒介（例如，本案中的互联网发帖）就违反第一修正案。†

†在 Packingham v. North Carolina 案中，最高法院 (Supreme Court) 在判决意见的附带说明 (dicta) 中将互联网等同于公共街道和公园，但从未明确裁定互联网是一个公共论坛。目前有几起涉及此问题的案件正在下级法院审理中。

（选项 C）是否存在可替代的沟通渠道是评估内容中立的言论限制（即对时间、地点或方式的限制）时的一个考量因素。但由于本法规是一项基于内容的限制，其保留了互联网以外沟通渠道这一事实是无关紧要的。

（选项 D）该法规或许能阻止雇员从事不道德的行为（例如，泄露商业秘密）。但无论如何，它都是违宪的，因为它无法通过严格审查。

教学目标：基于内容的言论限制被推定为无效，只有在通过严格审查时才能被维持——即，政府必须证明该限制是为了实现某一重大的政府利益所必需且经过严格限缩的。

References

United States v. Playboy Entm't Grp., 529 U.S. 803, 816 - 17 (2000) (explaining that content-based restrictions on speech require the government to satisfy strict scrutiny).
