data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

宪法：平等保护与基本权利
✅ 正确答案：A 州政府必须证明该法律对于实现紧迫的政府利益 (Compelling Government Interest) 是必要的 (Necessary)。
⚖️ 核心考点：严格审查标准

本题考察的是宪法中的平等保护条款 (Equal Protection Clause) 以及审查标准的分级。

解题的关键逻辑如下：

  1. 识别权利： 题目涉及的是婚姻权 (Right to Marry)。
  2. 定性权利： 在美国宪法下，婚姻权被视为基本权利 (Fundamental Right)。
  3. 确定标准： 当一项法律直接且实质性地干扰基本权利时，法院必须适用最高级别的审查标准，即严格审查 (Strict Scrutiny)。
📊 审查标准金字塔 (Standard of Review)
标准 适用对象 举证责任
严格审查
Strict Scrutiny		 基本权利 (婚姻、投票等)
可疑分类 (种族、国籍)		 政府证明：
1. 紧迫利益
2. 手段必要/限制最小
中度审查
Intermediate Scrutiny		 准可疑分类
(性别、非婚生子女)		 政府证明：
1. 重要利益
2. 实质性关联
合理依据
Rational Basis		 其他所有情况
(如年龄、财富、智力)		 原告证明：
无合理依据
🏛️ 经典判例：Zablocki v. Redhail (1978)

本题的案情与 Zablocki v. Redhail 案几乎完全一致。

在该案中，最高法院裁定：虽然收取子女抚养费是重要的政府利益，但禁止欠费者结婚并不是实现该利益的必要手段 (Necessary Means)（政府可以通过扣工资等限制较少的方法追债）。因此，该法律未能通过严格审查，被判违宪。

❌ 排除干扰项

选项 B (中度审查)： 仅适用于性别 (Gender) 或非婚生子女 (Legitimacy) 的分类，不适用于限制基本权利的情况。

选项 C & D (合理依据审查)： 这两种表述都属于 Rational Basis Test。在这种标准下，举证责任在原告（女性），且政府只需有“合理依据”。但这不适用于涉及基本权利（婚姻）的案件。

💡 MBE 提分技巧：
看到“婚姻 (Marriage)”、“投票 (Voting)”、“种族 (Race)”受限，大脑中应立即亮起红灯：Strict Scrutiny。

接着寻找对应的关键词：
  • 举证责任在政府 (State)
  • 利益必须是紧迫的 (Compelling)
  • 手段必须是必要的 (Necessary) 或 限制最小的 (Least Restrictive)

questions.question:
A state law increased the minimum hourly wage that employers are required to pay their employees by 12 percent. The law was enacted to address a variety of economic problems in the state, including the substantial need to pay persons a living wage. The owner of a retail store was assessed a fine for violating the law. The owner sincerely believes that God does not want him to increase the minimum hourly wage he pays his employees because a person's increase in wealth should result from an increase in faith as opposed to governmental action.
Is the law unconstitutional as applied to the owner?

choices.a: No, because the generally applicable law interferes with the owner's religious practices only incidentally.
choices.b: No, because the law is necessary to achieve the state's compelling interest in ensuring that persons receive a living wage.
choices.c: Yes, because the law unreasonably burdens the owner's free exercise of religion.
choices.d: Yes, because the state cannot dispute the sincerity of a person's religious beliefs.

questions.question:
A state prohibits voting for a write-in candidate in both primary and general elections. However, the state provides a mechanism by which individuals who want to appear as candidates on the primary ballot, as well as groups that want to be classified as a party, can do so.
Of the following, which is the best argument that a voter challenging the constitutionality of this ban on write-in candidates can make?

choices.a: The Fifteenth Amendment limits a state's power to regulate its own elections.
choices.b: The mechanism provided by the state does not provide for reasonable access to the ballot.
choices.c: The right to vote is a fundamental right, so the state ban is subject to strict scrutiny review.
choices.d: The state ban imposes a burden on the right of voters to select the candidates of their choice.

questions.question:
A clerical worker has been employed for the past two years in a permanent position in the county public records office in a state. The clerk has been responsible for copying and filing records of real estate transactions in that office. The clerk works in a nonpublic part of the office and has no contact with members of the public. However, state law provides that all real estate records in that office are to be made available for public inspection.
On the day an attempted assassination of the state's governor was reported on the radio, the clerk remarked to a coworker, "Our governor is such an evil man, I am sorry they did not get him." The coworker reported this remark to their employer, the county recorder. After the clerk admitted making the remark, the county recorder dismissed him stating that "there is no room in this office for a person who hates the governor so much."
The clerk sued for reinstatement and back pay. His only claim is that the dismissal violated his constitutional rights.
What will the court likely hold?

choices.a: The case is nonjusticiable, because public employment is a privilege rather than a right and, therefore, the clerk lacked standing to bring this suit.
choices.b: The dismissal was constitutional, because the compelling interest of the state in having loyal and supportive employees outweighs the interest of any state employee in his or her job or in free speech on a matter of public concern.
choices.c: The dismissal was unconstitutional, because in light of the clerk's particular employment duties, his right to express himself on a matter of public concern outweighed any legitimate interest the state might have had in discharging him.
choices.d: The dismissal was unconstitutional, because it constitutes a taking without just compensation of the clerk's property interest in his permanent position with the county.

data.questionStem:
Q82160

A clerical worker has been employed for the past two years in a permanent position in the county public records office in a state. The clerk has been responsible for copying and filing records of real estate transactions in that office. The clerk works in a nonpublic part of the office and has no contact with members of the public. However, state law provides that all real estate records in that office are to be made available for public inspection.

On the day an attempted assassination of the state's governor was reported on the radio, the clerk remarked to a coworker, "Our governor is such an evil man, I am sorry they did not get him." The coworker reported this remark to their employer, the county recorder. After the clerk admitted making the remark, the county recorder dismissed him stating that "there is no room in this office for a person who hates the governor so much."

The clerk sued for reinstatement and back pay. His only claim is that the dismissal violated his constitutional rights.

What will the court likely hold?

一名文员在某州的县公共记录办公室担任永久性职位已两年。该文员负责在该办公室复印和归档房地产交易记录。该文员在办公室的非公共区域工作，不与公众接触。然而，州法律规定，该办公室的所有房地产记录都应向公众开放查阅。

在电台报道该州州长遭遇未遂暗杀的当天，该文员对一位同事说：“我们的州长真是个恶棍，我很遗憾他们没得手。”同事将此言论报告给了他们的雇主，即县记录员。在该文员承认发表此言论后，县记录员将其解雇，并称“本办公室容不下如此憎恨州长的人”。

该文员提起诉讼，要求复职和补发薪资。他唯一的主张是，解雇侵犯了他的宪法权利。

法院可能会如何裁决？
options:
A. The case is nonjusticiable, because public employment is a privilege rather than a right and, therefore, the clerk lacked standing to bring this suit.
本案不可诉，因为公职是一种特权而非权利，因此，该文员缺乏提起此诉讼的诉讼资格。

B. The dismissal was constitutional, because the compelling interest of the state in having loyal and supportive employees outweighs the interest of any state employee in his or her job or in free speech on a matter of public concern.
该解雇是合宪的，因为州政府在拥有忠诚和支持性雇员方面的强大利益，超过了任何州雇员在其工作或就公共关注事务发表自由言论方面的利益。

C. The dismissal was unconstitutional, because in light of the clerk's particular employment duties, his right to express himself on a matter of public concern outweighed any legitimate interest the state might have had in discharging him.
该解雇是违宪的，因为鉴于该文员的特定工作职责，他就公共关注事务表达自己意见的权利，超过了州政府在解雇他方面可能拥有的任何合法利益。

D. The dismissal was unconstitutional, because it constitutes a taking without just compensation of the clerk's property interest in his permanent position with the county.
该解雇是违宪的，因为它构成了对该文员在县里永久性职位中所拥有的财产利益的无偿征用，而未给予公正补偿。
data.explanation:
The First Amendment right to free speech , applied to the states through the Fourteenth Amendment, does not extend to public employees speaking pursuant to their official duties. Therefore, the government can freely discipline or terminate employees for the content of their employment-related speech. But since this right does extend to public employees speaking as private citizens , the government can only regulate the content of that speech if its interest in efficient government function outweighs the employee's free speech right.

Here, the clerk was fired for remarking that he was sorry that the governor had not been assassinated. But the clerk spoke as a private citizen because his comment was made to a single coworker and was unrelated to his job duties - copying and filing real estate records with no public interaction. And since there is no indication that his comment impeded government efficiency, his right to express himself on this matter of public concern outweighs any legitimate state interest in discharging him. Therefore, the dismissal will likely be held unconstitutional.

(Choice A) To have a justiciable claim, a plaintiff must have standing - ie, suffered an injury-in-fact (unemployment) caused by the challenged action (termination) and redressable by the remedy sought (reinstatement and back pay). The fact that public employment is a privilege rather than a right is irrelevant.

(Choice B) The state's compelling interest in loyal and supportive employees does not outweigh a government employee's right to free speech on a matter of public concern (as seen here). But the state's interest will always outweigh an employee's right to free speech on a matter of private concern (eg, co-worker grievances).

(Choice D) The Fifth Amendment takings clause prohibits the government from taking private property for public use without just compensation. Under this clause, private property includes real property and personal property - but not the clerk's property interest in continuing public employment.

Educational objective: The government may regulate private speech by a public employee if the government's legitimate interest in efficient government function outweighs the employee's right to free speech.



选项正确率统计：A选项 6%，B选项 10%，C选项 67%（正确选项），D选项 14%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

《第一修正案》中的言论自由权通过《第十四修正案》适用于各州，但该权利不适用于公职人员履行其公务职责时发表的言论。因此，政府可以因雇员与工作相关的言论内容而自由地对其进行纪律处分或解雇。但由于该权利确实适用于作为普通公民发言的公职人员，因此，只有当政府在高效运作方面的利益超过雇员的言论自由权时，政府才能规制该言论的内容。

在本案中，该文员因表示对州长未被暗杀感到遗憾而被解雇。但该文员是以普通公民身份发言，因为他的评论是向单个同事发表的，并且与他的工作职责——复印和归档房地产记录，且不与公众互动——无关。由于没有迹象表明他的评论妨碍了政府效率，他在此公共关注事务上表达自己意见的权利，超过了州政府在解雇他方面的任何合法利益。因此，该解雇很可能被裁定为违宪。

(选项 A) 要提出可诉的请求，原告必须具有诉讼资格——即，遭受了由被质疑的行为（解雇）造成的事实上的损害（失业），并且该损害可通过所寻求的补救措施（复职和补发薪资）得到纠正。公职是特权而非权利这一事实与此无关。

(选项 B) 州政府在拥有忠诚和支持性雇员方面的强大利益，并不能超过政府雇员就公共关注事务发表自由言论的权利（如本案所示）。但州政府的利益将始终超过雇员就私人关注事务（例如，同事间的抱怨）发表自由言论的权利。

(选项 D) 《第五修正案》的征用条款禁止政府在没有公正补偿的情况下为公共用途征用私人财产。根据该条款，私人财产包括不动产和动产——但不包括该文员在持续公职中的财产利益。

教学目标：如果政府在高效运作方面的合法利益超过了公职人员的言论自由权，政府可以规制该雇员的私人言论。

References

Rankin v. McPherson, 483 U.S. 378, 388 - 90 (1987) (discussing when a government employee can be punished for speaking as a private citizen).

MBE 考点解析

宪法：第一修正案与公职人员
正确答案：C 法院很可能判定解雇违宪。因为文员就公共关注事务（Public Concern）发表言论的权利，在此案中超过了政府维持运作效率的利益。
⚖️ 核心法律规则：Pickering 平衡测试

当政府作为雇主（Public Employer）试图因言论惩罚雇员时，法院使用 Pickering-Connick Balancing Test 进行分析：

  • 1
    是否涉及公共关注 (Matter of Public Concern)？
    言论是否涉及政治、社会或其他社区关注的话题？如果是私人恩怨，政府通常可以自由惩罚。
  • 2
    是否作为普通公民发言 (Speaking as a Private Citizen)？
    言论是否属于其工作职责的一部分？如果是履行职责时的言论（如写官方报告），不受第一修正案保护。
  • 3
    利益衡量 (The Balancing)
    雇员的言论自由权益 vs. 政府提供高效公共服务的利益。
🗣️
雇员权益
就公共事务（州长遇刺）发表意见
>
🏢
政府利益
办公室效率、纪律、公众形象
🔍 本案深度解析

本题改编自真实判例 Rankin v. McPherson (1987)，案情几乎完全一致。

为何选 C？

  • 公共关注： 评论州长遇刺未遂显然是政治话题，属于公共关注。
  • 私人身份： 文员是对同事私下闲聊，并非在履行复印文件的职责。
  • 平衡结果：
    1. 文员职位低微（Clerical worker），不制定政策。
    2. 在非公共区域工作，不接触公众。
    3. 只是私下对同事说，没有造成办公室混乱。
    结论： 政府没有足够的理由（Compelling Interest）去压制这种言论。
❌ 干扰项排除
选项 A (特权论): 错误。 这是一个过时的法律概念。虽然没有“获得公职的权利”，但一旦受雇，政府不能以侵犯宪法权利（如言论自由）为由解雇员工。这被称为 Unconstitutional Conditions Doctrine。
选项 B (忠诚度): 错误。 政府对“忠诚”的要求通常仅限于制定政策的高级官员（Policymaking positions）或执法人员。对于一个不接触公众的低级文员，要求其政治观点与州长一致是不合理的。
选项 D (征用条款): 错误。 Takings Clause（第五修正案）通常涉及不动产或动产。虽然公职可以构成“财产权益”从而触发正当程序（Due Process）听证会，但解雇本身不被视为需要金钱补偿的“征用”。
💡 考试技巧：
遇到公职人员言论题，先看职位高低和言论内容。如果是低级职员谈论政治话题且未造成实际破坏，通常受宪法保护。

questions.question:
A federal statute requires all males between the ages of 18 and 26 to register with the Selective Service Agency, which is responsible for drafting individuals to serve in the armed forces in the event of war. The statute makes it a felony to fail to register but provides an exemption for individuals who hold a sincere religious objection to war. The statute allows the federal government to question the sincerity and reasonableness of religious objections. The provisions of the statute are inseverable.
An 18-year-old man applying for federal student loans noted on the loan application that he had not registered with the Selective Service Agency. A representative of the Agency contacted the man, and the man said that he had no intention of registering due to his religious belief that all war is wrong. After refusing to register on several more occasions, the man was arrested and charged under the federal statute.
What is the man's strongest argument that the federal statute is unconstitutional?

choices.a: The statute denies him the equal protection of the laws because it only applies to men.
choices.b: The statute denies him the equal protection of the laws because it only applies to those between the ages of 18 and 26.
choices.c: The statute violates his right to freely exercise his religious beliefs by allowing the government to challenge the reasonableness of those beliefs.
choices.d: The statute violates his right to freely exercise his religious beliefs by allowing the government to challenge the sincerity of those beliefs.

data.questionStem:
Q82165

A federal statute requires all males between the ages of 18 and 26 to register with the Selective Service Agency, which is responsible for drafting individuals to serve in the armed forces in the event of war. The statute makes it a felony to fail to register but provides an exemption for individuals who hold a sincere religious objection to war. The statute allows the federal government to question the sincerity and reasonableness of religious objections. The provisions of the statute are inseverable.

An 18-year-old man applying for federal student loans noted on the loan application that he had not registered with the Selective Service Agency. A representative of the Agency contacted the man, and the man said that he had no intention of registering due to his religious belief that all war is wrong. After refusing to register on several more occasions, the man was arrested and charged under the federal statute.

What is the man's strongest argument that the federal statute is unconstitutional?

一项联邦法规要求所有年龄在18至26岁之间的男性在 Selective Service Agency（兵役登记局）进行登记，该机构负责在战争时征召个人入伍服役。该法规将未登记者定为重罪，但为因真诚的宗教信仰而反对战争的个人提供了豁免。该法规允许联邦政府质疑宗教反对意见的真诚性（sincerity）和合理性（reasonableness）。该法规的条款不可分割。

一名18岁男子在申请联邦助学贷款时，在贷款申请表上注明他未在 Selective Service Agency 登记。该机构的一名代表联系了该男子，该男子表示，由于他宗教信仰认为所有战争都是错误的，因此他无意登记。在又几次拒绝登记后，该男子被逮捕并根据该联邦法规被起诉。

该男子能提出的、主张该联邦法规违宪的最有力论点是什么？
options:
A. The statute denies him the equal protection of the laws because it only applies to men.
该法规仅适用于男性，因此剥夺了法律对他的平等保护。

B. The statute denies him the equal protection of the laws because it only applies to those between the ages of 18 and 26.
该法规仅适用于18至26岁的人群，因此剥夺了法律对他的平等保护。

C. The statute violates his right to freely exercise his religious beliefs by allowing the government to challenge the reasonableness of those beliefs.
该法规允许政府挑战其宗教信仰的合理性，从而侵犯了他自由行使其宗教信仰的权利。

D. The statute violates his right to freely exercise his religious beliefs by allowing the government to challenge the sincerity of those beliefs.
该法规允许政府挑战其宗教信仰的真诚性，从而侵犯了他自由行使其宗教信仰的权利。
data.explanation:
The First Amendment free exercise clause prohibits the government from punishing an individual for any sincerely held religious belief. As a result, any government inquiry is limited to whether a professed belief is sincere - not whether that belief is reasonable or true (Choice D). Here, the federal statute allows the government to challenge the reasonableness of any religious objection to Selective Service registration. Therefore, this is the man's strongest argument that the federal statute is unconstitutional.

(Choice A) A federal law that intentionally discriminates based on gender or legitimate birth violates the equal protection component of the Fifth Amendment unless it passes intermediate scrutiny. This standard of scrutiny is likely met here because, as the U.S. Supreme Court held in Rostker v. Goldberg, the male-only requirement is substantially related to the government's important interest in national defense.

(Choice B) Under the Fifth Amendment's equal protection component, a federal law that does not impact a fundamental right or protected class is generally valid under mere rational basis scrutiny. Age is not a protected class, so the statute's application to those between the ages of 18 and 26 is likely valid.

Educational objective: The free exercise clause allows the government to question whether a religious belief is sincerely held but not whether that belief is reasonable or true.



选项正确率统计：A选项 8%，B选项 1%，C选项 57%（正确选项），D选项 31%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

First Amendment 的 free exercise clause（宗教自由行使条款）禁止政府因个人持有的任何真诚的宗教信仰而对其进行惩罚。因此，任何政府的审查仅限于所声称的信仰是否真诚——而不是该信仰是否合理或真实（选项D）。在本案中，该联邦法规允许政府挑战对 Selective Service 登记的任何宗教反对意见的合理性。因此，这是该男子主张该联邦法规违宪的最有力论点。

（选项A）一项基于性别或合法出生进行有意歧视的联邦法律，违反了 Fifth Amendment 的平等保护部分，除非它通过了中度审查（intermediate scrutiny）。在本案中，这一审查标准很可能得到满足，因为正如美国最高法院在 Rostker v. Goldberg 案中所裁定的那样，仅限男性的要求与政府在国防方面的重要利益有实质性关联。

（选项B）根据 Fifth Amendment 的平等保护部分，一项不影响基本权利或受保护阶层的联邦法律，在仅需合理基础审查（rational basis scrutiny）的情况下通常是有效的。年龄不属于受保护阶层，因此该法规适用于18至26岁的人群很可能是有效的。

教学目标：free exercise clause 允许政府质疑宗教信仰是否为真诚持有，但不能质疑该信仰是否合理或真实。

References

  • United States v. Seeger, 380 U.S. 163, 184 - 85 (1965) (explaining that the government's only task is to determine whether a professed religious belief is sincerely held).
  • Rostker v. Goldberg, 453 U.S. 57, 78 - 79 (1981) (holding that a law exempting women from the draft does not violate the equal protection component of the Fifth Amendment).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考题解析

Constitutional Law | Individual Rights
正确答案：C
核心考点：宗教信仰的审查界限
Free Exercise Clause (自由行使条款)
根据美国宪法第一修正案，政府在审查宗教豁免申请时：
  • ✅ 可以审查信仰是否“真诚持有” (sincerely held)。
  • ❌ 绝对禁止审查信仰是否“合理” (reasonable) 或“真实” (true)。
为什么选 C？

本题的关键在于法规中的一句话：“The statute allows the federal government to question the sincerity and reasonableness of religious objections.”（该法规允许联邦政府质疑宗教反对意见的真诚性和合理性。）

法律推理：

  1. 真诚性 vs. 合理性： 最高法院在 United States v. Ballard 等判例中确立，法院或政府机构不能充当宗教教义的仲裁者。如果政府试图判断一个人的宗教信仰是否符合逻辑、是否“合理”，这就直接违反了第一修正案。
  2. 违宪性： 题目中的法规明确授权政府审查信仰的“合理性”，这是对 Free Exercise Clause 的直接侵犯。
  3. 不可分割性 (Inseverability)： 题目特别提到条款是不可分割的。这意味着，一旦“审查合理性”这一条款被认定违宪，整个法规（或其对该男子的适用）就站不住脚了。

因此，攻击该法规允许审查“合理性”，是该男子最致命、最直接的宪法论据。

为什么其他选项不是最强论点？
选项 A：性别歧视 (Equal Protection)
虽然基于性别的分类需要通过中度审查 (Intermediate Scrutiny)，但在 Rostker v. Goldberg (1981) 案中，最高法院已经裁定：仅要求男性进行兵役登记不违宪。法院认为这与政府在国防上的重要利益有实质性关联。因此，这不是一个赢面大的论点。
选项 B：年龄歧视 (Equal Protection)
年龄不是“受保护阶层” (Suspect Class)。针对年龄的分类只需通过合理基础审查 (Rational Basis Review)。政府征召适龄青年入伍显然是理性的。这个论点非常弱。
选项 D：审查真诚性 (Sincerity)
这是一个常见的陷阱。法律允许政府审查信仰是否“真诚”。如果一个人只是为了逃避兵役而撒谎说自己信教，政府有权揭穿谎言。因此，攻击政府审查“真诚性”的权力是无效的。
💡 MBE 考试技巧
在涉及宗教自由的题目中，看到政府试图评估宗教信仰的“真理” (truth)、“有效性” (validity) 或 “合理性” (reasonableness) 时，这通常就是违宪的“死穴”。记住：Sincerity (真诚) 可查，Truth (真理) 免谈。

questions.question:
A state law makes it a criminal offense for any state employee to "knowingly provide educational services or extend welfare benefits" to a foreign national who was in the United States in violation of U.S. immigration laws. The principal of a public elementary school, who is a U.S. citizen, is prosecuted under the law for enrolling and providing education to several foreign nationals he knew to be in the country illegally. All of these actions took place before the law was adopted. No federal statute applied to the principal's actions.
What constitutional provision would be most helpful to the principal's defense?

choices.a: The due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.
choices.b: The equal protection clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.
choices.c: The ex post facto clause of Article I, Section 10.
choices.d: The privileges or immunities clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.

data.questionStem:
Q82102

A state law makes it a criminal offense for any state employee to "knowingly provide educational services or extend welfare benefits" to a foreign national who was in the United States in violation of U.S. immigration laws. The principal of a public elementary school is prosecuted under the law for enrolling and providing education to several foreign nationals he knew to be in the country illegally. All of these actions took place before the law was adopted. No federal statute applied to the principal's actions.

What constitutional provision would be most helpful to the principal's defense?

一项州法律规定，任何州雇员“明知而向违反美国移民法居留在美国的外国国民提供教育服务或扩大福利”的行为构成刑事犯罪。一所公立小学的校长因招收几名他明知为非法居留该国的外国国民并为其提供教育而根据该法被起诉。所有这些行为都发生在该法律通过之前。没有任何联邦法规适用于该校长的行为。

哪一项宪法条款对该校长的辩护最有帮助？
options:
A. The due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.
第十四修正案的正当程序条款。

B. The equal protection clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.
第十四修正案的平等保护条款。

C. The ex post facto clause of Article I, Section 10.
Article I, Section 10 的事后法条款。

D. The privileges or immunities clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.
第十四修正案的特权或豁免条款。
data.explanation:
Ex post facto clauses


(applies to federal (art. 1, § 9) & state (art. 1, § 10) governments) Prohibit enactment of retroactive criminal laws that:
  • criminalize previously legal conduct
  • impose greater punishment than previously prescribed
  • eliminate previously available defenses
  • decrease prosecution's previous burden of proof
The Article I, § 10 ex post facto clause prohibits state governments from enacting retroactive criminal laws - eg, laws that punish conduct that occurred before the law became effective (thereby criminalizing previously legal conduct). And because the principal enrolled foreign nationals before the law under which he is being prosecuted was adopted, the ex post facto clause would be most helpful to his defense.

(Choice A) The Fourteenth Amendment due process clause requires that states enact reasonable laws. Laws that substantially burden a fundamental right are only reasonable if they pass strict scrutiny - which rarely occurs. But since the principal has no fundamental right to enroll foreign nationals in his school, this law need only pass rational basis scrutiny - which is easily done. Therefore, due process would not be helpful to his defense.

(Choice B) The equal protection clause prohibits states from enacting laws that treat similarly situated people differently (as seen here). But since this state law does not substantially impact a fundamental right or protected class, the law need only pass rational basis scrutiny - ie, be rationally related to any legitimate government interest. Therefore, an equal protection challenge would likely fail.

(Choice D) The Fourteenth Amendment privileges or immunities clause prohibits states from infringing on the very limited rights of national citizenship - none of which are at issue here.

Educational objective: The ex post facto clauses prohibit federal and state governments from enacting retroactive criminal laws - eg, laws that punish conduct that occurred before the law became effective.

选项正确率统计：A选项 4%，B选项 14%，C选项 80%（正确选项），D选项 1%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

事后法条款


（适用于联邦（Article 1, § 9）和州（Article 1, § 10）政府）禁止制定具有溯及力的刑法，这些法律：
  • 将先前合法的行为定为犯罪
  • 施加比先前规定更重的惩罚
  • 取消先前可用的抗辩理由
  • 降低检方先前的证明责任
Article I, § 10 的事后法条款禁止州政府制定具有溯及力的刑法——例如，惩罚在法律生效之前发生的行为的法律（从而将先前合法的行为定为犯罪）。而且，由于校长是在他被起诉所依据的法律通过之前招收外国国民的，因此事后法条款对他的辩护最有帮助。

（选项 A）第十四修正案的正当程序条款要求各州制定合理的法律。对基本权利构成实质性负担的法律，只有通过严格审查（strict scrutiny）才被认为是合理的——这种情况很少发生。但由于校长没有在其学校招收外国国民的基本权利，该法只需通过理性基础审查（rational basis scrutiny）即可——这很容易做到。因此，正当程序对他的辩护没有帮助。

（选项 B）平等保护条款禁止各州制定区别对待处境相似的人的法律（如此处所见）。但由于这项州法律并未对基本权利或受保护阶层产生实质性影响，该法只需通过理性基础审查即可——即，与任何合法的政府利益有理性关联。因此，基于平等保护的质疑很可能会失败。

（选项 D）第十四修正案的特权或豁免条款禁止各州侵犯非常有限的国民公民权——此处并未涉及其中任何权利。

教学目标：事后法条款禁止联邦和州政府制定具有溯及力的刑法——例如，惩罚在法律生效之前发生的行为的法律。

References

Lindsey v. Washington, 301 U.S. 397, 401 (1937) (explaining that the ex post facto clause "forbids the application of any new punitive measure to a crime already consummated").

MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law / Individual Rights

✅ 正确答案：C

Article I, Section 10 的事后法条款 (Ex Post Facto Clause) 是对该校长最有利的辩护依据。

核心考点：事后法 (Ex Post Facto Laws)

美国宪法明确禁止联邦政府（Article I, § 9）和州政府（Article I, § 10）制定事后法。根据最高法院在 Calder v. Bull (1798) 中的定义，违反该条款的法律包括：

  1. 将先前合法的行为定为犯罪 (Criminalizing past innocent conduct)。
  2. 加重对先前犯罪行为的惩罚 (Aggravating the punishment)。
  3. 改变证据规则以降低定罪门槛 (Altering rules of evidence)。
案情时间线分析
步骤 1：行为发生
校长招收了外国国民并提供教育。
当时该行为并未被该州法律定为犯罪。
步骤 2：法律通过
州政府通过新法，将此类行为定为刑事犯罪。
步骤 3：提起诉讼
检察官试图用新法起诉旧的行为。

结论： 既然校长的行为发生在法律通过之前，州政府试图用新法惩罚旧行为，这正是宪法绝对禁止的“具有溯及力的刑法适用” (Retroactive application of criminal law)。

为什么其他选项不是最佳？
❌ A & B: 正当程序 (Due Process) 与 平等保护 (Equal Protection)
虽然该法律可能因为剥夺受教育权或基于国籍的歧视而面临第十四修正案的挑战（参考 Plyler v. Doe 案），但这些挑战需要复杂的法律分析（如审查标准 Scrutiny Levels）。
相比之下，事后法条款提供了一个绝对的、程序性的防御：无论法律内容是否合宪，它都不能适用于法律生效前发生的行为。这是最直接、最“有帮助”的辩护。
❌ D: 特权或豁免条款 (Privileges or Immunities Clause)
该条款在历史上被最高法院（屠宰场案 Slaughter-House Cases）解释得非常狭窄，主要仅涉及作为美国公民的权利（如跨州迁徙权），几乎从未成功用于此类刑事辩护。
💡 MBE 考试技巧 当题目中出现“时间差”（行为在前，立法在后）且涉及刑事处罚 (Criminal Offense) 时，请立即联想 Ex Post Facto Clause。这是宪法题中送分题的典型特征。

questions.question:
Under a state law, a drug company that makes a false factual claim about a prescription drug is strictly liable in tort to any user of the drug.
In an advertisement promoting sales of a particular drug, a drug company claimed that the drug was safe for children. Suit was filed against the company on behalf of a child who allegedly was harmed as a result of taking the drug. At the time the child took the drug, the available medical studies supported the company's claim that the drug was safe for children, but later research proved that the drug actually was harmful to children. The company has moved to dismiss the suit on First Amendment grounds.
Should the court grant the motion?

choices.a: No, because false or misleading commercial speech is not constitutionally protected.
choices.b: No, because the drug business is subject to extensive health and safety regulation.
choices.c: Yes, because liability cannot be imposed for false statements without a showing of actual malice.
choices.d: Yes, because the company's claims about the drug were a matter of public concern.

Should the court grant the motion?

根据州法律，一家制药公司若对其处方药作出虚假事实陈述，则需对任何该药品的使用者承担侵权法上的严格责任。

在一则旨在推广某特定药品的广告中，一家制药公司声称该药品对儿童是安全的。后有人代表一名据称因服用该药而受到伤害的儿童对该公司提起了诉讼。在该儿童服药之时，现有的医学研究支持该公司关于药品对儿童安全的说法，但后来的研究证明该药品实际上对儿童有害。该公司已基于 First Amendment 的理由，动议驳回此项诉讼。

法院是否应批准该动议？
options:
A. No, because false or misleading commercial speech is not constitutionally protected.
不应，因为虚假或误导性的商业言论不受宪法保护。

B. No, because the drug business is subject to extensive health and safety regulation.
不应，因为制药行业受到广泛的健康和安全法规的约束。

C. Yes, because liability cannot be imposed for false statements without a showing of actual malice.
应该，因为若无实际恶意的证明，不得因虚假陈述而施加责任。

D. Yes, because the company's claims about the drug were a matter of public concern.
应该，因为该公司关于药品的声明是公众关注的事项。
data.explanation:
Commercial speech is speech that does no more than propose a commercial transaction (eg, advertisements). Although this type of speech is afforded some First Amendment protections , these protections do not extend to commercial speech that
  • is false or misleading
  • concerns unlawful activity
- even if these statements are made without knowledge or reckless disregard of their falsity or illegality (ie, without actual malice) (Choice C).

Here, the company's advertisement innocently claimed that its drug was safe for children. But this advertisement lost any First Amendment protections when later research proved that the company's drug safety claim was false. Therefore, the company's motion to dismiss the false advertisement suit on First Amendment grounds should be denied.

(Choice B) The fact that the drug business is subject to extensive health and safety regulation does not exclude its speech from First Amendment protections.

(Choice D) Commercial speech that is false or misleading (as seen here) or concerns unlawful activity never receives First Amendment protection, regardless of whether that speech pertains to a matter of public concern.

Educational objective: The First Amendment does not protect commercial speech that
  • is false or misleading
  • concerns unlawful activity
- regardless of whether the speaker knew (or recklessly disregarded) that the speech was false, misleading, or unlawful.



选项正确率统计：A选项 78%（正确选项），B选项 5%，C选项 11%，D选项 5%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

商业言论是指仅为提议一项商业交易的言论（例如，广告）。尽管此类言论享有一定的First Amendment 保护，但这些保护并不适用于以下商业言论：
  • 虚假或误导性的言论
  • 涉及非法活动的言论
——即便作出这些陈述时并不知道其虚假性或非法性，也非鲁莽漠视其虚假性或非法性（即没有实际恶意）（选项C）。

在本案中，该公司的广告无过错地声称其药品对儿童是安全的。但当后来的研究证明该公司的药品安全声明是虚假的，这则广告便失去了任何 First Amendment 的保护。因此，该公司以 First Amendment 为由动议驳回虚假广告诉讼的请求应被否决。

（选项B）制药行业受到广泛的健康和安全法规约束这一事实，并不能将其言论排除在 First Amendment 的保护之外。

（选项D）虚假或误导性（如本案所示）或涉及非法活动的商业言论，无论其是否与公众关注的事项有关，都绝不会获得 First Amendment 的保护。

教学目标：First Amendment 不保护以下商业言论：
  • 虚假或误导性的言论
  • 涉及非法活动的言论
——无论言论发表者是否知道（或鲁莽漠视）该言论是虚假、误导或非法的。

References

Cent. Hudson Gas & Elec. Corp. v. Pub. Serv. Comm'n, 447 U.S. 557, 566 (1980) (explaining that false and misleading commercial speech is not protected by the First Amendment).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

宪法第一修正案与商业言论

正确答案：A

本题考察的核心是商业言论（Commercial Speech）在宪法第一修正案（First Amendment）下的保护范围，特别是当言论被证明为虚假时的情况。

⚖️ 核心法律规则

根据最高法院在 Central Hudson Gas & Elec. Corp. v. Public Service Commission 案中确立的标准，商业言论要获得第一修正案的保护，必须满足首要条件：

该言论必须涉及合法活动，且不得是虚假或误导性的。

如果商业言论是虚假的（False）或误导性的（Misleading），它将完全不受第一修正案的保护。

🔍 案情分析

1. 言论性质：
制药公司的广告属于典型的Commercial Speech（以促进商业交易为目的）。

2. 关键事实：
尽管公司在发布广告时依据了当时的医学研究（主观上无恶意），但后来的研究证明“药品对儿童安全”这一声明在客观事实上是虚假的。

3. 结论：
因为该商业言论在事实上是虚假的，所以它失去了第一修正案的保护伞。州政府可以依据法律对发布虚假广告的公司实施严格责任（Strict Liability），而无需考虑公司当时是否知情。

🚫 为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 C 错误（最大干扰项）：
选项 C 提到了“实际恶意”（Actual Malice）。这是诽谤法中针对公职人员（Public Officials）的标准（源自 NYT v. Sullivan）。

在商业言论领域，只要陈述是虚假的，政府就可以监管或惩罚，不需要证明发布者有实际恶意（即明知虚假或鲁莽漠视真相）。制药公司不能因为“当时不知道是假的”而免责。
选项 B 错误：
虽然制药业确实受到严格监管，但这并不是驳回动议的直接法律依据。核心理由是言论本身的“虚假性”剥夺了宪法保护，而不是因为行业受监管。
选项 D 错误：
即使药品安全是“公众关注的事项”（Matter of Public Concern），这一属性也不能为虚假的商业广告提供保护伞。虚假商业言论在宪法上没有价值。
💡 MBE 考试技巧

遇到涉及广告、促销的 First Amendment 题目时，请按以下步骤思考：

  1. 这是商业言论吗？（是的，广告）。
  2. 言论是否虚假、误导或涉及非法产品？
    • 如果是 ➡️ 无宪法保护（政府可以随意禁止/惩罚）。
    • 如果否 ➡️ 应用 Central Hudson 测试的后续步骤（政府利益是否实质性？限制手段是否直接推进利益且不过度？）。

questions.question:
A city owned and operated a municipal bus system. The city sold space on its buses for the posting of placards. Under the relevant city ordinance, the administrator of the bus system had sole discretion to decide which placards could be posted on the buses, and the administrator's decision was final. Although most of the placards that appeared on city buses were commercial advertisements, the administrator had often sold space on the buses for placards promoting various political, charitable, and religious causes.
After a circus bought space on the buses for placards advertising its upcoming performances, an animal rights organization asked to buy space for a placard with photographs showing the mistreatment of animals in circus shows.
The administrator denied the organization's request, stating that the proposed placard would be offensive to the circus, which had paid a substantial sum to place its placards on the buses, and that a circus employee had told her that none of the photographs on the organization's placard depicted animals belonging to this particular circus.
The organization sued the administrator in an appropriate court for a declaration that her denial of the organization's request for placard space for the reasons she gave violated the First Amendment as made applicable to the states by the Fourteenth Amendment.
Is the organization likely to prevail?

choices.a: No, because a public official may not allow the use of public facilities for the propagation of a message that he or she believes may create a false or misleading impression.
choices.b: No, because the administrator's denial of space to the organization was a reasonable time, place, and manner restriction of speech.
choices.c: Yes, because a public official may not refuse to allow the use of any public facility to publish a message dealing with an issue of public concern.
choices.d: Yes, because a public official may not refuse to permit the dissemination of a message in a public forum solely on the basis of its content unless that denial is necessary to serve a compelling government interest.

一个城市拥有并运营一个市政公交系统。该市出售其公交车上的空间用于张贴标语牌。根据相关城市法令，公交系统的管理员拥有决定哪些标语牌可以在公交车上张贴的独有裁量权，且管理员的决定是最终的。尽管城市公交车上出现的大多数标语牌是商业广告，但管理员也经常出售公交车上的空间，用于张贴宣传各种政治、慈善和宗教事业的标语牌。

在一个马戏团购买了公交车空间以张贴广告宣传其即将到来的表演后，一个动物权利组织请求购买空间，用于张贴一张带有马戏团表演中动物受虐待照片的标语牌。

管理员拒绝了该组织的请求，理由是该组织提议的标语牌会冒犯马戏团，因为马戏团已支付大笔费用在公交车上张贴其标语牌，并且一名马戏团员工告诉她，该组织标语牌上的照片没有一张描绘的是属于这个特定马戏团的动物。

该组织在适当的法院起诉了管理员，请求法院宣告，她基于所给出的理由拒绝该组织张贴标语牌空间的请求，违反了通过Fourteenth Amendment适用于各州的First Amendment。

该组织是否可能胜诉？
options:
A. No, because a public official may not allow the use of public facilities for the propagation of a message that he or she believes may create a false or misleading impression.
不会，因为公职人员不得允许使用公共设施来传播他或她认为可能产生虚假或误导性印象的信息。

B. No, because the administrator's denial of space to the organization was a reasonable time, place, and manner restriction of speech.
不会，因为管理员拒绝该组织的空间请求是对言论的合理的时间、地点和方式的限制。

C. Yes, because a public official may not refuse to allow the use of any public facility to publish a message dealing with an issue of public concern.
会，因为公职人员不得拒绝允许使用任何公共设施来发布涉及公共关注问题的信息。

D. Yes, because a public official may not refuse to permit the dissemination of a message in a public forum solely on the basis of its content unless that denial is necessary to serve a compelling government interest.
会，因为公职人员不得仅因其内容而拒绝在公共论坛上传播信息，除非该拒绝是为了服务于紧迫的政府利益所必需的。
data.explanation:
Forum-based regulation of speech


TypesDefinitionRegulations
Traditional public forumsPublic property historically used for, or associated with, public speech (eg, streets, sidewalks, parks)Content-based regulations prohibited
Designated (limited) public forumsPublic property opened for specific types of expression (eg, school classrooms, civic auditoriums)
Nonpublic forumsAll other public propertyContent-based regulations permitted if viewpoint-neutral
The First Amendment prohibits the government from engaging in content-based discrimination against different categories of speech - even in public forums. Therefore, government censorship of speech based solely on its message (or what is said) will only be upheld if the government can satisfy the strict scrutiny test. This requires the government to prove that its actions are necessary and narrowly tailored to achieve a compelling government interest.

Here, the administrator for the municipal bus system denied the animal rights organization's request to buy space for a placard with photos of mistreated circus animals. Her stated reasoning was that the content of that placard would offend the circus and the photos on its placard did not depict animals belonging to that circus. And since this constitutes content-based discrimination that is unlikely to pass strict scrutiny, the organization will likely prevail.

(Choice A) The government can limit the use of public facilities for commercial speech (eg, an advertisement placard) that creates a false or misleading impression since that speech is not protected by the First Amendment. But it cannot limit the use of public facilities for non- commercial speech - even if it is false or misleading - since that amounts to a content-based restriction subject to strict scrutiny.

(Choice B) The administrator's denial of space was based on the content - not the time, place, or manner - of the organization's message. However, reasonable time, place, and manner restrictions can be imposed in designated public forums - ie, public property opened for public expression - like the bus.

(Choice C) A public official engages in content-based regulation by refusing to allow the use of a public facility to publish a message that addresses a public concern. But this refusal is permitted in nonpublic forums so long as it is viewpoint neutral - ie, denies discussion on all sides of the issue.

Educational objective: The government can only impose content-based restrictions on speech in public forums if the government can satisfy the strict scrutiny test - ie, prove that the restriction is necessary to achieve a compelling government interest.

选项正确率统计：A选项 4%，B选项 11%，C选项 1%，D选项 82%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

基于论坛的言论规制


类型定义规制
传统公共论坛历史上用于或与公众言论相关的公共财产（例如，街道、人行道、公园）基于内容的规制被禁止
指定（有限）公共论坛为特定类型的表达而开放的公共财产（例如，学校教室、市政礼堂）
非公共论坛所有其他公共财产如果观点中立，则基于内容的规制被允许
First Amendment禁止政府对不同类别的言论进行基于内容的歧视——即使是在公共论坛中。因此，政府仅基于信息内容（即所言为何）对言论进行审查，只有在政府能够满足严格审查（strict scrutiny）标准时才会被支持。这要求政府证明其行为是为实现紧迫的政府利益所必需且是狭义限定的。

在本案中，市政公交系统的管理员拒绝了动物权利组织购买空间以张贴带有受虐待马戏团动物照片的标语牌的请求。她陈述的理由是，该标语牌的内容会冒犯马戏团，且其标语牌上的照片并未描绘属于该马戏团的动物。由于这构成了基于内容的歧视，且不大可能通过严格审查，因此该组织很可能胜诉。

(选项A) 政府可以限制公共设施用于产生虚假或误导性印象的商业言论（例如，广告标语牌），因为该言论不受First Amendment的保护。但政府不能限制公共设施用于非商业言论——即使其内容是虚假或误导性的——因为这构成了一种基于内容的限制，需接受严格审查。

(选项B) 管理员拒绝提供空间是基于该组织信息的内容——而非时间、地点或方式。然而，在指定的公共论坛——即为公众表达而开放的公共财产——如本案的公交车上，可以施加合理的时间、地点和方式限制。

(选项C) 公职人员拒绝允许使用公共设施发布涉及公共关注问题的信息，这是一种基于内容的规制。但这种拒绝在非公共论坛中是允许的，只要它是观点中立的——即，拒绝就该议题的各方观点进行讨论。

教学目的： 政府只有在能够满足严格审查标准的情况下，才能在公共论坛上对言论施加基于内容的限制——即，证明该限制是为实现紧迫的政府利益所必需的。

MBE 考点解析

宪法第一修正案：言论自由与公共论坛

Constitutional Law First Amendment

本题考察的核心是公共论坛理论 (Public Forum Doctrine) 以及政府在不同类型的论坛中限制言论的审查标准。

核心考点：指定公共论坛 (Designated Public Forum) 当政府自愿将其财产开放给公众进行广泛的表达活动（如政治、宗教言论）时，该财产即成为"指定公共论坛"。在此类论坛中，政府对言论的限制受到与"传统公共论坛"（如街道、公园）相同的严格限制。

逻辑推演步骤

1
定性论坛类型：
题目指出，虽然公交车主要用于商业广告，但管理员经常出售空间用于政治、慈善和宗教事业。这表明政府已将该广告空间开放为指定公共论坛 (Designated Public Forum)。
2
识别限制性质：
管理员拒绝广告是因为它会"冒犯"马戏团（内容/观点）以及照片的具体内容。这是典型的基于内容 (Content-Based) 的限制。
3
适用审查标准：
在公共论坛中，基于内容的限制必须通过严格审查 (Strict Scrutiny)。
标准：必须是为了实现紧迫的政府利益 (Compelling Interest) 且手段是必要 (Necessary) 的。
4
得出结论：
避免冒犯商业客户（马戏团）并非"紧迫的政府利益"。因此，该限制违宪。
论坛类型 基于内容的限制标准
传统/指定公共论坛
(Public Forum)		 严格审查 (Strict Scrutiny)
需证明紧迫利益 (Compelling Interest)
非公共论坛
(Nonpublic Forum)		 合理性审查 (Reasonableness)
且必须观点中立 (Viewpoint Neutral)
✅ 正确答案：选项 D

Yes, because a public official may not refuse to permit the dissemination of a message in a public forum solely on the basis of its content unless that denial is necessary to serve a compelling government interest.

解析：这是对严格审查标准的准确描述。由于公交车广告位已成为指定公共论坛，政府不能仅因不喜欢广告内容（基于内容）而拒绝刊登，除非能通过严格审查。本案中政府无法通过此测试。

为什么其他选项是错误的？

  • 选项 A (False/Misleading)： 虽然政府可以监管虚假的商业言论，但本案涉及的是政治/公益言论（动物权利），享有最高级别的保护。此外，仅凭马戏团员工的一面之词就认定"误导"，且以此为由进行事前限制（Prior Restraint），是不合法的。
  • 选项 B (Time, Place, Manner)： 合理的时间、地点和方式限制 (TPM) 必须是内容中立 (Content-Neutral) 的。本案中，拒绝是因为广告的"冒犯性"内容，因此不属于 TPM 限制。
  • 选项 C (Public Concern)： 这个选项表述过于绝对。在非公共论坛中，政府实际上可以拒绝某些涉及公共关注议题的讨论，只要这种拒绝是合理的且观点中立的（例如，军事基地可以禁止所有政治演讲）。本题的关键在于论坛的性质（公共论坛）触发了严格审查。
MBE 备考助手 | 宪法篇

questions.question:
A number of psychotherapists routinely send mailings to victims of car accidents informing the victims of the possibility of developing post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) as the result of the accidents, and offering psychotherapy services. Although PTSD is a possible result of a car accident, it is not common.
Many accident victims in a particular state who received the mailings complained that the mailings were disturbing and an invasion of their privacy. These victims also reported that as a result of the mailings, their regard for psychotherapists and for psychotherapy as a form of treatment had diminished. In response, the state enacted a law prohibiting any licensed psychotherapist from sending mailings that raised the concern of PTSD to any car accident victim in the state until 30 days after the accident. The state justified the law as an effort to address the victims' complaints as well as to protect the reputation of psychotherapy as a form of treatment.
Is this law constitutional?

choices.a: No, because the law singles out one type of message for prohibition while allowing others.
choices.b: No, because the mailings provide information to consumers.
choices.c: Yes, because mailings suggesting the possibility of developing PTSD as the result of an accident are misleading.
choices.d: Yes, because the law protects the privacy of accident victims and the public regard for psychotherapy without being substantially more restrictive than necessary.

Q82060

A number of psychotherapists routinely send mailings to victims of car accidents informing the victims of the possibility of developing post- traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) as the result of the accidents, and offering psychotherapy services. Although PTSD is a possible result of a car accident, it is not common.

Many accident victims in a particular state who received the mailings complained that the mailings were disturbing and an invasion of their privacy. These victims also reported that as a result of the mailings, their regard for psychotherapists and for psychotherapy as a form of treatment had diminished. In response, the state enacted a law prohibiting any licensed psychotherapist from sending mailings that raised the concern of PTSD to any car accident victim in the state until 30 days after the accident. The state justified the law as an effort to address the victims' complaints as well as to protect the reputation of psychotherapy as a form of treatment.

Is this law constitutional?

一些心理治疗师定期向车祸受害者寄送邮件，告知他们因事故有可能会患上创伤后应激障碍（PTSD），并提供心理治疗服务。虽然PTSD是车祸可能导致的后果，但这并不常见。

在某州，许多收到此类邮件的车祸受害者抱怨这些邮件令人不安，并侵犯了他们的隐私。这些受害者还报告称，由于这些邮件，他们对心理治疗师以及作为一种治疗方式的心理治疗的尊重程度有所下降。作为回应，该州颁布了一项法律，禁止任何有执照的心理治疗师在事故发生后30天内，向州内的任何车祸受害者发送引起PTSD担忧的邮件。该州为该法律辩护称，此举是为了回应受害者的投诉，并保护心理治疗作为一种治疗方式的声誉。

该法律是否合宪？
options:
A. No, because the law singles out one type of message for prohibition while allowing others.
不合宪，因为该法律单独禁止一种信息，却允许其他信息。

B. No, because the mailings provide information to consumers.
不合宪，因为这些邮件向消费者提供了信息。

C. Yes, because mailings suggesting the possibility of developing PTSD as the result of an accident are misleading.
合宪，因为暗示因事故可能患上PTSD的邮件具有误导性。

D. Yes, because the law protects the privacy of accident victims and the public regard for psychotherapy without being substantially more restrictive than necessary.
合宪，因为该法律在保护事故受害者隐私和公众对心理治疗的尊重的同时，其限制性并未实质上超出必要范围。
data.explanation:
Commercial speech encompasses all types of economically-oriented expression (eg, advertisements). And it receives intermediate First Amendment protection so long as it is not false or misleading and does not concern unlawful activity. Therefore, government regulation of protected commercial speech is only constitutional if it
  • directly advances a substantial government interest and
  • is narrowly drawn - ie, not substantially more restrictive than necessary - to serve that interest.


Here, the state law prohibits psychotherapists from sending mailings about PTSD (including offers of services) to car-accident victims within 30 days of their accidents. These commercial mailings concern a lawful activity and are not false or misleading since they only suggest the possibility (not the likelihood) of developing PTSD (Choice C). And since a 30-day waiting period
  • directly advances the state's substantial interests in protecting victims' privacy and psychotherapy's reputation and
  • is not substantially more restrictive than necessary, the law is constitutional.


(Choice A) Laws that prohibit one type of message while allowing others (ie, content-based restrictions) are generally struck down under strict scrutiny. But since the state law concerns commercial speech - which only undergoes intermediate scrutiny - it permissibly targets PTSD mailings.

(Choice B) The mailings are protected commercial speech because they seek to provide consumers with information about PTSD - not to mislead them. But the government can still regulate the content of the mailings because the regulation meets intermediate scrutiny.

Educational objective: Commercial speech that is false/misleading or concerns unlawful activity can be freely regulated. But any other commercial speech can only be regulated if the government shows, under intermediate scrutiny, that its regulation
  • directly advances a substantial government interest and
  • is narrowly drawn to serve that interest.




选项正确率统计：A选项 20%，B选项 1%，C选项 6%，D选项 71%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

商业言论包含所有类型的经济导向的表达（例如，广告）。只要其内容并非虚假或具有误导性，且不涉及非法活动，它就会受到First Amendment（第一修正案）的中度保护。因此，政府对受保护的商业言论的规制，只有在满足以下条件时才合宪：
  • 直接促进重大的政府利益，并且
  • 为服务于该利益而精准制定——即限制性没有实质上超出必要范围。


在本案中，州法律禁止心理治疗师在车祸发生30天内向受害者发送关于PTSD的邮件（包括提供服务的要约）。这些商业邮件涉及合法活动，并且不具虚假性或误导性，因为它们只暗示了患上PTSD的可能性（而非概然性）（选项C）。并且，由于这30天的等待期
  • 直接促进了州政府在保护受害者隐私和心理治疗声誉方面的重大利益，并且
  • 其限制性没有实质上超出必要范围，因此该法律是合宪的。


（选项A）禁止一种信息而允许其他信息的法律（即基于内容的限制）通常会在严格审查下被推翻。但由于该州法律涉及商业言论——仅需经过中度审查——因此可以被允许地针对有关PTSD的邮件。

（选项B）这些邮件是受保护的商业言论，因为它们旨在向消费者提供有关PTSD的信息，而不是误导他们。但政府仍然可以规制这些邮件的内容，因为该规制满足中度审查标准。

教学目标：虚假/误导性或涉及非法活动的商业言论可以被自由规制。但任何其他商业言论只有在政府通过中度审查证明其规制满足以下条件时，才能被规制：
  • 直接促进一项重大的政府利益，并且
  • 为服务于该利益而精准制定。


References

Fla. Bar v. Went for It, Inc., 515 U.S. 618, 634 - 35 (1995) (upholding a state bar rule prohibiting attorneys from mailing solicitations to car-accident victims for 30 days after their accidents).

MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Commercial Speech
⚖️ 核心法则：Central Hudson Test

对于商业言论 (Commercial Speech)，政府的规制必须通过中度审查 (Intermediate Scrutiny)。根据 Central Hudson 案确立的标准，规制合宪需满足以下四点：

  1. 言论必须涉及合法活动且不具误导性 (Protected Speech)。
  2. 政府必须主张一项重大的利益 (Substantial Interest)。
  3. 规制必须直接促进该利益 (Directly Advance)。
  4. 规制手段必须精准制定，即限制性没有实质上超出必要范围 (Narrowly Drawn / Reasonable Fit)。
🔍 题目解析

本题改编自美国最高法院的著名判例 Florida Bar v. Went For It, Inc. (1995)。

1. 言论性质：
心理治疗师的邮件属于商业言论。题目明确指出PTSD是“可能的后果”，因此邮件内容并非虚假或误导性 (Not misleading)，属于受宪法第一修正案保护的言论。

2. 政府利益：
州政府提出了两项利益：(1) 保护受害者隐私；(2) 保护该行业的声誉。法院认定这些属于重大的政府利益 (Substantial Interest)。

3. 手段的合理性：
法律仅禁止在事故后30天内发送邮件。这并非永久禁止，而是一个短暂的“冷却期”。这种限制直接缓解了受害者在创伤初期的困扰，且没有过度限制言论自由（治疗师仍可以通过其他方式广告，或在30天后联系）。这符合“限制性未实质上超出必要范围”的要求。

✅ 正确答案：D
正确理由

D 选项完美复述了商业言论审查的后半部分标准。它指出了法律保护了隐私（重大利益），且限制手段（30天禁令）没有实质上超出必要范围（Narrowly Drawn）。

❌ 错误选项速览
选项 A

错误点：虽然这是“基于内容的限制” (Content-based)，但在商业言论领域，只要满足中度审查，政府可以针对特定内容的商业广告进行规制。严格审查 (Strict Scrutiny) 通常不适用于商业言论。

选项 B

错误点：虽然邮件提供了信息，但这并不意味着它享有绝对豁免权。只要通过了 Central Hudson 测试，提供信息的商业言论依然可以被限制。

选项 C

错误点：题目事实已说明PTSD是“可能的”后果，因此邮件内容在法律上不构成误导。如果言论本身是误导性的，政府可以直接禁止，无需进行后续的利益平衡测试。

💡 MBE 提分技巧：
看到“律师/医生/专业人士”向“事故受害者”发送“邮件/信件”的题目：
  • 如果是面对面 (In-person) 招揽生意：通常可以完全禁止（因为存在压迫和欺诈风险）。
  • 如果是邮件 (Mail)：通常受保护，但政府可以设置合理的时间限制（如本题的30天）来保护隐私。
  • 关键词记忆：Commercial Speech = Intermediate Scrutiny。

questions.question:
A Senate investigative committee released a report identifying three U.S. citizens as individuals who were organizing support for terrorist activities. All three were employed by the U.S. government as park rangers.
In response, Congress enacted a statute naming these three individuals and providing that they could not hold any position of employment with the federal government.
Which of the following constitutional provisions provides the best means for challenging the constitutionality of the statute?

choices.a: The bill of attainder clause.
choices.b: The due process clause.
choices.c: The ex post facto clause.
choices.d: The takings clause.

data.questionStem:
Q82146

A Senate investigative committee released a report identifying three U.S. citizens as individuals who were organizing support for terrorist activities. All three were employed by the U.S. government as park rangers.

In response, Congress enacted a statute naming these three individuals and providing that they could not hold any position of employment with the federal government.

Which of the following constitutional provisions provides the best means for challenging the constitutionality of the statute?

一个参议院调查委员会发布了一份报告，指认三名美国公民为组织支持恐怖主义活动的个人。

这三人均受雇于美国政府，担任公园管理员。

作为回应，国会颁布了一项法案，点名这三名个人，并规定他们不得担任联邦政府的任何雇佣职位。

以下哪项宪法条款为挑战该法案的合宪性提供了最佳依据？
options:
A. The bill of attainder clause.
剥夺公权的法案条款 (bill of attainder clause)。

B. The due process clause.
正当程序条款 (due process clause)。

C. The ex post facto clause.
追溯既往的法律条款 (ex post facto clause)。

D. The takings clause.
征收条款 (takings clause)。
data.explanation:
Prohibited legislation


Bill of attainder clausesProhibit legislative acts that inflict civil or criminal punishment against identified persons (or groups of persons) without a trial
Ex post facto clausesProhibit enactment of retroactive criminal laws that:
  • criminalize previously legal conduct
  • impose greater punishment than previously prescribed
  • eliminate previously available defenses
  • decrease prosecution's previous burden of proof
The Article I bill of attainder clauses prohibit federal and state legislative acts that inflict civil or criminal punishment on named persons - or easily identifiable groups of persons - without a judicial trial. Here, the federal statute bars three named park rangers from federal government employment. And since this constitutes a civil punishment that is imposed without a trial, the statute is an unconstitutional bill of attainder.

(Choice B) The Fifth Amendment due process clause requires the government to provide persons with notice and a meaningful opportunity to be heard before depriving them of a life, liberty, or property interest. Public employment is a property interest when the employee:
  • has an ongoing employment contract,
  • can only be fired for cause, or
  • receives assurances of continued employment
- none of which apply here.

(Choice C) The ex post facto clauses bar legislative acts that impose retroactive criminal punishments - ie, punish conduct that occurred before the law was enacted. Although the rangers' alleged support of terrorism occurred before the statute was enacted, their exclusion from government employment is a civil punishment.

(Choice D) The Fifth Amendment takings clause prohibits the government from taking private property for public use without just compensation. But this clause applies to real or personal property - not interests in public employment.

Educational objective: The bill of attainder clauses prohibit legislative acts that inflict civil or criminal punishment on named individuals - or easily identifiable groups of individuals - without a trial. Exclusion from a profession or vocation is a type of civil punishment.

选项正确率统计：A选项 65%（正确选项），B选项 27%，C选项 4%，D选项 2%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

被禁止的立法


剥夺公权的法案条款禁止未经审判即对已确定身份的个人（或群体）施加民事或刑事处罚的立法行为
追溯既往的法律条款禁止制定具有追溯效力的刑事法律，这些法律：
  • 将以前的合法行为定为犯罪
  • 施加比以前规定更严厉的处罚
  • 取消以前可用的抗辩理由
  • 降低检方以前的证明责任
美国宪法第一条中的剥夺公权的法案 (bill of attainder) 条款禁止联邦和州采取立法行为，在未经司法审判的情况下，对被点名的个人——或易于识别的个人群体——施加民事或刑事处罚。在本案中，联邦法案禁止三名被点名的公园管理员受雇于联邦政府。由于这构成了未经审判而施加的民事处罚，因此该法案是违宪的剥夺公权的法案。

(选项 B) 第五修正案的正当程序条款要求政府在剥夺个人的生命、自由或财产利益之前，必须向其提供通知和有意义的听证机会。当雇员存在以下情况时，公共雇佣关系构成一种财产利益：
  • 拥有持续的雇佣合同，
  • 只能因故被解雇，或
  • 获得了持续雇佣的保证
——这些情况在本案中均不适用。

(选项 C) 追溯既往的法律条款禁止施加具有追溯效力的刑事处罚的立法行为——即处罚在法律颁布前已发生的行为。尽管这些公园管理员被指控支持恐怖主义的行为发生在该法案颁布之前，但将他们从政府雇佣中排除是一种民事处罚。

(选项 D) 第五修正案的征收条款禁止政府在未给予公正补偿的情况下为公共用途征用私有财产。但该条款适用于不动产或个人财产——不适用于公共雇佣关系中的利益。

教学目标：剥夺公权的法案 (bill of attainder) 条款禁止未经审判即对被点名的个人——或易于识别的个人群体——施加民事或刑事处罚的立法行为。被排除于某一行业或职业之外是一种民事处罚。

References

  • U.S. Const. art. I, § 9 (prohibits the federal government from enacting bills of attainder).
  • United States v. Lovett, 328 U.S. 303, 315 - 16 (1946) (holding that a congressional act that excludes a specific person from a profession or vocation without a trial is an unconstitutional bill of attainder).

MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights
核心考点：剥夺公权法案

Bill of Attainder Clause (U.S. Const. art. I, § 9)

宪法禁止国会通过任何未经司法审判即对特定个人或群体施加惩罚的立法。

🔍 题目逻辑分析

本题的三个关键要素完全符合 Bill of Attainder 的定义：

  1. 特定对象 (Specificity)： 法案直接点名了三位具体的个人 (naming these three individuals)。
  2. 施加惩罚 (Punishment)： 禁止他们在联邦政府任职。最高法院已裁定，永久性禁止从事某种职业属于一种“惩罚”。
  3. 无司法审判 (No Trial)： 这是由立法机关（国会）直接判定的，而非通过法院的司法程序。

因此，挑战该法案合宪性的最佳依据是 Bill of Attainder Clause。

经典判例 (Key Precedent)

United States v. Lovett (1946)

本题的情节几乎直接取材于该案。在该案中，国会通过法案切断了三名被指控从事“颠覆活动”的政府雇员的薪水。最高法院裁定，这种针对特定个人并将其排除在政府服务之外的立法行为，构成了违宪的 Bill of Attainder。

❌ 为什么其他选项不是最佳？
(B) Due Process (正当程序)
虽然未经听证就解雇可能涉及程序性正当程序问题，但 Bill of Attainder 是更具体、更直接的宪法障碍。当立法机关试图扮演法官的角色时，首先触犯的是剥夺公权法案条款。
(C) Ex Post Facto (追溯既往)
该条款通常仅适用于刑事法规的追溯。虽然失去工作是一种“惩罚”，但在 Ex Post Facto 的语境下，它通常被视为民事或监管性质，而非严格的刑事惩罚。相比之下，Bill of Attainder 对“惩罚”的定义更宽泛，包括剥夺就业资格。
(D) Takings Clause (征收条款)
政府职位通常不被视为可以通过征收条款获得金钱补偿的“私有财产”。
💡 MBE 考试技巧
当你看到题目中出现“立法机关通过法律点名惩罚特定人”（Legislature passes a law naming individuals...）的情节时，请立即联想 Bill of Attainder。

这是立法权侵犯司法权的典型表现。

questions.question:
A state law imposed a generally applicable sales tax payable by the vendor. That law exempted from its provisions the sale of "all magazines, periodicals, newspapers, and books." In order to raise additional revenue, the state legislature eliminated that broad exemption and substituted a narrower exemption. The new, narrower exemption excluded from the state sales tax only the sale of those "magazines, periodicals, newspapers, and books that are published or distributed by a state-recognized religious faith and that consist wholly of writings sacred to such a religious faith."
A magazine devoted to history and politics paid under protest the sales tax due on its sales according to the amended sales tax law. The magazine then filed suit against the state in an appropriate state court for a refund of the sales taxes paid. It contended that the state's elimination of the earlier, broader exemption and adoption of the new, narrower exemption restricted to sacred writings of state-recognized religious faiths violates the First and Fourteenth Amendments to the Constitution.
In this case, how will the court likely rule?

choices.a: The Eleventh Amendment bars the state court from exercising jurisdiction over this suit in the absence of a state law expressly waiving the state's immunity.
choices.b: The magazine lacks standing to sue for a refund of sales taxes imposed by a generally applicable state law because Article III of the Constitution precludes taxpayers from bringing such suits.
choices.c: The new, narrower exemption from the state sales tax law violates the establishment clause of the First and Fourteenth Amendments by granting preferential state support to religious faiths recognized by the state.
choices.d: The new, narrower exemption from the state sales tax law violates the freedom of the press guaranteed by the First and Fourteenth Amendments because it imposes a prior restraint on nonreligious publications that are required to pay the tax.

一部州法规定了一项普遍适用的销售税，由销售商支付。该法将其条款豁免于“所有杂志、期刊、报纸和书籍”的销售。为了增加额外收入，州立法机构取消了这项宽泛的豁免，并代之以一项更窄的豁免。这项新的、更窄的豁免仅将那些“由州政府认可的宗教信仰出版或发行，且完全由对此类宗教信仰而言是神圣的著作组成”的“杂志、期刊、报纸和书籍”的销售排除在州销售税之外。

一家专注于历史和政治的杂志根据修订后的销售税法，在抗议下支付了其销售额应缴的销售税。该杂志随后在适当的州法院对州政府提起诉讼，要求退还已支付的销售税。该杂志主张，州政府取消先前的宽泛豁免，并采纳仅限于州政府认可的宗教信仰的神圣著作的新的、更窄的豁免，违反了《宪法》第一修正案和第十四修正案。

在本案中，法院可能会如何裁决？
options:
A. The Eleventh Amendment bars the state court from exercising jurisdiction over this suit in the absence of a state law expressly waiving the state's immunity.
在没有州法律明确放弃州豁免权的情况下，第十一修正案禁止州法院对本诉讼行使管辖权。

B. The magazine lacks standing to sue for a refund of sales taxes imposed by a generally applicable state law because Article III of the Constitution precludes taxpayers from bringing such suits.
该杂志缺乏诉讼资格，不能就一项普遍适用的州法所征收的销售税要求退款提起诉讼，因为《宪法》第三条禁止纳税人提起此类诉讼。

C. The new, narrower exemption from the state sales tax law violates the establishment clause of the First and Fourteenth Amendments by granting preferential state support to religious faiths recognized by the state.
州销售税法中新的、更窄的豁免，通过为州政府认可的宗教信仰提供优先的国家支持，违反了第一修正案和第十四修正案的国教条款。

D. The new, narrower exemption from the state sales tax law violates the freedom of the press guaranteed by the First and Fourteenth Amendments because it imposes a prior restraint on nonreligious publications that are required to pay the tax.
州销售税法中新的、更窄的豁免违反了第一修正案和第十四修正案所保障的新闻自由，因为它对需要缴税的非宗教出版物施加了事先限制。

Courts may apply strict scrutiny if government directly benefits/burdens religion.

Government benefits to religious organizations must comply with the First Amendment establishment clause, which applies to the states through the Fourteenth Amendment. Challenges brought under this clause are generally reviewed under the historical test. However, courts may forego this test and apply the more stringent strict scrutiny test when the law directly benefits or burdens a particular religion. Under strict scrutiny, the law is invalid unless the government proves that the law is necessary to achieve a compelling government interest.

Here, the new sales tax exemption applies only to sacred writings published or distributed by religious faiths recognized by the state. This exemption directly benefits state-recognized religions and burdens unrecognized religions, so strict scrutiny applies. And since it is unlikely that the state will be able to show that granting preferential state support to state-recognized religious faiths is necessary to achieve a compelling interest, the court will likely rule that the exemption violates the establishment clause.

(Choice A) The Eleventh Amendment bars private parties (and foreign governments) from suing a state in federal court without the state's express consent. But since the magazine sued in state court, the Eleventh Amendment does not apply.

(Choice B) Article III's standing requirement only applies to federal courts. But even if it applied to state courts, taxpayers do have standing to sue the government for sales tax refunds or any other issue regarding taxes owed if that injury is redressable by the remedy sought.

(Choice D) Prior restraints are a form of government censorship that bans publication before it occurs. As a result, they are unconstitutional absent exceptional circumstances (eg, national security). Here, the tax exemption is not a prior restraint since it does not prohibit publication.

Educational objective:
Establishment clause challenges are generally reviewed under the historical test. But strict scrutiny can be used instead when a law directly benefits or burdens a particular religion. In that case, the law is invalid unless the government proves that the law is necessary to achieve a compelling government interest.

选项正确率统计：A选项 7%，B选项 6%，C选项 78%（正确选项），D选项 7%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

如果政府直接有益于或加重宗教负担，法院可适用严格审查。

政府给予宗教组织的利益必须遵守第一修正案的国教条款（establishment clause），该条款通过第十四修正案适用于各州。根据该条款提起的挑战通常在历史测试下进行审查。然而，当法律直接有益于或加重特定宗教的负担时，法院可以放弃此测试，并适用更严格的严格审查（strict scrutiny）标准。在严格审查标准下，除非政府能证明该法律对于实现重大的政府利益是必要的，否则该法律无效。

在本案中，新的销售税豁免仅适用于由州政府认可的宗教信仰出版或发行的神圣著作。此豁免直接有益于州政府认可的宗教，同时加重了未被认可的宗教的负担，因此适用严格审查。并且，由于州政府不大可能证明，为实现重大利益而必须向州政府认可的宗教信仰提供优先的国家支持，法院很可能裁定该豁免违反了国教条款。

(选项A) 第十一修正案禁止私人当事方（及外国政府）在未经州政府明确同意的情况下，在联邦法院起诉州政府。但由于该杂志是在州法院提起诉讼，第十一修正案不适用。

(选项B) 第三条的诉讼资格（standing）要求仅适用于联邦法院。但即使它适用于州法院，如果纳税人所受的损害可以通过寻求的救济措施得到弥补，那么他们确实有资格就销售税退款或任何其他有关应缴税款的问题起诉政府。

(选项D) 事先限制（Prior restraints）是政府审查的一种形式，它在出版物发行前就禁止其发行。因此，除非有特殊情况（例如，国家安全），否则它们是违宪的。在本案中，该税收豁免并非事先限制，因为它并未禁止出版。

教学目标：
针对国教条款的挑战通常根据历史测试进行审查。但当一项法律直接有益于或加重特定宗教的负担时，可以转而使用严格审查标准。在这种情况下，除非政府证明该法律对于实现重大的政府利益是必要的，否则该法律无效。

References

Texas Monthly, Inc. v. Bullock, 489 U.S. 1, 14–15, 20 (1989) (holding that preferential tax exemptions solely for religious groups violate the establishment clause).

Larson v. Valente, 456 U.S. 228, 246 (1982) (explaining that strict scrutiny applies to laws that aid or prefer one religion).

MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law / 宪法
✅ 正确答案：C

该豁免违反了第一修正案的国教条款 (Establishment Clause)。

核心考点：政府的中立性

第一修正案国教条款禁止政府制定任何“确立宗教”的法律。这要求政府在宗教与非宗教之间，以及不同宗教派别之间保持中立 (Neutrality)。

本案中，州政府取消了普遍适用的豁免，改为仅针对“州认可的宗教信仰”的神圣著作进行免税。这种做法存在两个致命的宪法缺陷：

  1. 偏袒宗教而非世俗： 它给予宗教出版物优于世俗出版物（如历史政治杂志）的特殊待遇。
  2. 教派偏袒 (Sect Preference)： 它仅豁免“州认可”的宗教，这涉及政府对宗教真伪或地位的审查，直接歧视未被认可的宗教。
审查标准：严格审查

当一项法律在表面上区分不同宗教，或给予宗教相对于非宗教的特殊优惠时，法院通常适用严格审查 (Strict Scrutiny)。

政府必须证明该法律是：

  • 为了实现重大的政府利益 (Compelling Government Interest)；且
  • 手段是必要的 (Necessary) 或狭义剪裁的 (Narrowly Tailored)。

在本案中，为了“增加收入”而歧视性地向特定宗教提供免税，显然无法通过严格审查。

参考判例：Texas Monthly, Inc. v. Bullock (1989) —— 最高法院裁定，仅针对宗教期刊的销售税豁免违宪，因为它缺乏世俗目的且具有支持宗教的效果。

为什么其他选项是错误的？

选项 A (第十一修正案): 错误。 第十一修正案 (11th Amendment) 限制的是私人公民在联邦法院起诉州政府。本案是在州法院提起的诉讼，因此第十一修正案不适用。
选项 B (诉讼资格 Standing): 错误。 虽然一般纳税人不能仅因“我是纳税人”就起诉政府乱花钱，但当纳税人被要求支付一项其认为违宪的税款时，他完全有资格提起退税诉讼。这是直接的经济损害 (Injury-in-fact)。
选项 D (事先限制 Prior Restraint): 错误。 事先限制通常指政府在出版前进行审查或禁止。销售税是一种事后负担，并非禁止出版。虽然歧视性税收违宪，但理由是违反国教条款或新闻自由中的非歧视原则，而不是因为它构成了“事先限制”。
💡 MBE 解题技巧 看到税收豁免仅适用于“宗教”或“特定宗教”时，警钟应立即响起。

如果政府给予广泛的慈善豁免（包括宗教、教育、医疗等），通常是合宪的（如 Walz 案）；但如果豁免专门且排他地给予宗教组织，而没有包含类似的世俗组织，这通常违反国教条款。

questions.question:
A state has a state employee grievance system that requires any state employee who wishes to file a grievance against the state to submit that grievance for final resolution to a panel of three arbitrators chosen by the parties from a statewide board of 13 arbitrators. In any given case, the grievant and the state alternate in exercising the right of each party to eliminate five members of the board, leaving a panel of three members to decide their case. At the present time, the full board is composed of seven male arbitrators and six female arbitrators.
A female state employee filed a sexual harassment grievance against her male supervisor and the state. The state's attorney exercised all of her five strikes to eliminate five of the female arbitrators. At the time she did so, the state's attorney stated that she struck the five female arbitrators solely because she believed women, as a group, would necessarily be biased in favor of another woman who was claiming sexual harassment. Counsel for the state employee eliminated four males and one female arbitrator, all solely on grounds of specific bias or conflicts of interest. As a result, the panel was all male.
When the panel ruled against the state employee on the merits of her case, she filed an action in an appropriate state court, challenging the panel-selection process as a gender-based denial of equal protection of the laws.
In this case, how should the court rule as to the constitutionality of the panel-selection process?

choices.a: Constitutional, because the gender classification used by the state's attorney in this case satisfies the requirements of the rational basis test.
choices.b: Constitutional, because the gender classification used by the state's attorney in this case satisfies the requirements of the strict scrutiny test.
choices.c: Unconstitutional, because the gender classification used by the state's attorney in this case denies the grievant the right to a jury made up of her peers.
choices.d: Unconstitutional, because the gender classification used by the state's attorney in this case does not satisfy the requirements of intermediate scrutiny.

某州设有一套州雇员申诉系统，该系统要求任何希望对州政府提出申诉的州雇员，必须将其申诉提交给一个由三名仲裁员组成的小组进行最终解决。这些仲裁员由当事人从一个由13名仲裁员组成的全州委员会中选出。在任何特定的案件中，申诉人和州政府轮流使用各自的权利，从委员会中排除五名成员，剩下三名成员组成小组来裁决他们的案件。目前，整个委员会由七名男性仲裁员和六名女性仲裁员组成。

一名女性州雇员对她的男性主管和州政府提起了性骚扰申诉。州政府的律师行使其全部五次排除权，排除了五名女性仲裁员。在行使该权利时，州政府律师声明，她排除这五名女性仲裁员的唯一原因是她认为，女性作为一个群体，必然会偏袒另一位声称受到性骚扰的女性。该州雇员的法律顾问则以特定偏见或利益冲突为由，排除了四名男性仲裁员和一名女性仲裁员。结果，仲裁小组全部由男性组成。

当该小组就案件的实体问题作出了不利于该州雇员的裁决后，她向有管辖权的州法院提起诉讼，质疑仲裁小组的遴选程序构成了基于性别的对法律平等保护的剥夺。

在本案中，法院应如何就仲裁小组遴选程序的合宪性作出裁决？
options:
A. Constitutional, because the gender classification used by the state's attorney in this case satisfies the requirements of the rational basis test.
合宪，因为本案中州政府律师所使用的性别分类满足了“理性基础测试”的要求。

B. Constitutional, because the gender classification used by the state's attorney in this case satisfies the requirements of the strict scrutiny test.
合宪，因为本案中州政府律师所使用的性别分类满足了“严格审查标准”的要求。

C. Unconstitutional, because the gender classification used by the state's attorney in this case denies the grievant the right to a jury made up of her peers.
违宪，因为本案中州政府律师所使用的性别分类剥夺了申诉人由其同辈组成的陪审团进行审理的权利。

D. Unconstitutional, because the gender classification used by the state's attorney in this case does not satisfy the requirements of intermediate scrutiny.
违宪，因为本案中州政府律师所使用的性别分类不满足“中度审查标准”的要求。
data.explanation:
Equal protection (standards of review)


StandardApplicabilityTest
Rational basisDefault testChallenger must show action is not rationally related to legitimate government interest
Intermediate scrutinyDiscriminates against quasi-suspect class: Sex/gender LegitimacyGovernment must show action is substantially related to important government interest
Strict scrutinyDiscriminates against suspect class (EARN): Ethnicity Alienage (state law only) Race Nationality

Impacts fundamental right (First VIP): First Amendment rights Voting Interstate travel Privacy: family, marriage, parental rights, sexual acts, contraceptives		Government must show action is necessary (ie, least restrictive means) to achieve compelling government interest
When a government action is challenged under the equal protection clause, it must survive intermediate scrutiny if it discriminates against a quasi-suspect class - ie, gender/sex, illegitimate birth. Intermediate scrutiny requires the state to prove that its action was substantially related to an important government interest.

Here, the state's attorney removed female arbitrators from the panel (government action) because she believed that women would be biased in favor of another woman claiming sexual harassment (gender discrimination). But as the Supreme Court reasoned in J.E.B. v. Alabama ex rel. T.B., a juror's or arbitrator's competence and impartiality (important government interest) cannot be evaluated based on gender (no substantial relationship). Therefore, the attorney's actions cannot survive intermediate scrutiny and should be ruled unconstitutional.

(Choice A) The rational basis test requires the challenger to prove that the government action has no rational relationship to a legitimate government interest. But since this test only applies when the government action does not affect a fundamental right, suspect class, or quasi- suspect class, it does not apply here.

(Choice B) Strict scrutiny requires the state to prove that its action is necessary to achieve a compelling government interest when it substantially impacts a fundamental right or suspect class - not a quasi-suspect class (as seen here).

(Choice C) Most criminal and civil litigants have the right to a jury made up of their peers - ie, an impartial group of citizens selected from a fair cross-section of the community. But this right does not apply to non-judicial proceedings like arbitration (as seen here).

Educational objective: Gender discrimination in the jury (or arbitrator) selection process cannot survive intermediate scrutiny since it is not substantially related to the government's important interest in having grievances decided by competent and impartial individuals. Therefore, such discrimination violates the equal protection clause.

选项正确率统计：A选项 4%，B选项 0%，C选项 16%，D选项 77%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

平等保护（审查标准）


标准适用性检验标准
理性基础默认检验标准质疑方必须证明该行为与合法的政府利益没有理性关联
中度审查歧视准可疑分类：性别/婚生地位政府必须证明该行为与重要的政府利益有实质性关联
严格审查歧视可疑分类 (EARN): Ethnicity (族裔) Alienage (外国人身份，仅州法) Race (种族) Nationality (国籍)

影响基本权利 (First VIP): First Amendment rights (第一修正案权利) Voting (投票权) Interstate travel (州际旅行权) Privacy (隐私权): 家庭、婚姻、父母权利、性行为、避孕		政府必须证明该行为为实现迫切的政府利益所必需（即限制最少的手段）
当一项政府行为根据平等保护条款受到质疑时，如果它歧视了准可疑分类——即性别、非婚生子女身份，那么它必须经受中度审查。中度审查要求州政府证明其行为与重要的政府利益有实质性关联。

在本案中，州政府律师将女性仲裁员从仲裁小组中排除（政府行为），因为她认为女性会偏袒另一位声称受到性骚扰的女性（性别歧视）。但正如最高法院在 J.E.B. v. Alabama ex rel. T.B. 案中所论述的，陪审员或仲裁员的能力和公正性（重要的政府利益）不能基于性别来评估（无实质性关联）。因此，该律师的行为无法通过中度审查，应被裁定为违宪。

(选项A) 理性基础测试要求质疑方证明政府行为与合法的政府利益没有理性关联。但由于该测试仅在政府行为不影响基本权利、可疑分类或准可疑分类时适用，因此在本案中不适用。

(选项B) 严格审查要求州政府在行为实质性影响基本权利或可疑分类时，证明其行为为实现迫切的政府利益所必需——而非本案中的准可疑分类。

(选项C) 大多数刑事和民事诉讼的当事方有权由其同辈组成的陪审团进行审理——即从社区的公正横断面上选出的一组公正的公民。但此项权利不适用于仲裁等非司法程序（如本案所示）。

教学目的：在陪审团（或仲裁员）遴选过程中的性别歧视无法通过中度审查，因为它与“由有能力且公正的个人来裁决申诉”这一重要的政府利益没有实质性关联。因此，这种歧视违反了平等保护条款。

References

  • U.S. Const. amend. XIV (equal protection clause).
  • J.E.B. v. Alabama ex rel. T.B., 511 U.S. 127, 136 (1994) (explaining that the government cannot rely on gender stereotypes to justify gender-based discrimination).

MBE 考点解析

Equal Protection & Gender Discrimination

Constitutional Law Individual Rights
核心考点：审查标准 (Standards of Review)

本题的核心在于判断针对性别 (Gender) 的政府分类应当适用何种宪法审查标准。在第十四修正案的平等保护条款 (Equal Protection Clause) 下，法院根据分类的性质适用不同层级的审查。

分类 (Class) 审查标准 (Standard) 举证责任
种族、国籍
(Suspect Class)		 严格审查
(Strict Scrutiny)		 政府
性别、非婚生子女
(Quasi-Suspect Class)		 中度审查
(Intermediate Scrutiny)		 政府
年龄、财富等
(Other)		 理性基础
(Rational Basis)		 原告
法律分析与判例
关键规则：
政府在陪审团或仲裁员遴选过程中，不得基于性别进行歧视。这种基于性别的分类必须通过中度审查 (Intermediate Scrutiny)。 参考判例: J.E.B. v. Alabama ex rel. T.B. (1994)

在本案中，州政府律师（State's Attorney）代表政府行事，构成了政府行为 (State Action)。她明确表示排除女性仲裁员是因为“女性会偏袒女性”。这构成了基于性别的分类。

根据中度审查标准，政府必须证明该分类与重要的政府利益 (Important Government Interest) 具有实质性关联 (Substantially Related)。

最高法院已明确裁定，基于刻板印象（如认为女性会因性别而产生偏见）并不构成正当理由。因此，这种做法无法通过中度审查。

✅ 正确答案：选项 D

违宪，因为本案中州政府律师所使用的性别分类不满足“中度审查标准”的要求。

这是唯一正确识别了适用于性别歧视的审查标准（中度审查）并得出正确结论（违宪）的选项。

为什么其他选项是错误的？
  • 选项 A (Rational Basis): 错误。理性基础测试适用于非可疑分类（如年龄、经济状况）。性别属于“准可疑分类”，标准更高。
  • 选项 B (Strict Scrutiny): 错误。严格审查适用于“可疑分类”（如种族 Race、国籍 National Origin）。性别歧视尚未上升到严格审查的高度。
  • 选项 C (Jury of Peers): 错误。
    1. 本案是仲裁 (Arbitration)，不是刑事或民事审判，通常没有宪法保障的陪审团权利。
    2. 即使有，本案的宪法争议点在于“平等保护”，而非第六或第七修正案的陪审团构成权利。
💡 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)

在 MBE 宪法题中，遇到平等保护 (Equal Protection) 问题时，请按以下步骤思考：

  1. 识别分类：政府是基于什么特征在区别对待？(本题是性别)
  2. 确定标准：该特征对应哪个审查等级？(性别 = 中度审查)
  3. 应用测试：政府的理由是否站得住脚？(刻板印象通常无法通过中度或严格审查)

questions.question:
A city operates a cemetery pursuant to a city ordinance. The ordinance requires the operation of the city cemetery to be supported primarily by revenues derived from the sale of cemetery lots to individuals. The ordinance further provides that the purchase of a cemetery lot entitles the owner to perpetual care of the lot, and entitles the owner to erect on the lot, at the owner's expense, a memorial monument or marker of the owner's choice, subject to certain size restrictions. The city ordinance requires the city to maintain the cemetery, including mowing the grass, watering flowers, and plowing snow, and provides for the expenditure of city tax funds for such maintenance if revenues from the sale of cemetery lots are insufficient.
Although cemetery lots are sold at full fair market value, which includes the current value of perpetual care, the revenue from the sale of such lots has been insufficient in recent years to maintain the cemetery. As a result, a small amount of city tax funds has also been used for that purpose.
A group of city taxpayers brings suit against the city challenging the constitutionality of the city ordinance insofar as it permits the owner of a cemetery lot to erect a religious memorial monument or marker on his or her lot.
Is this suit likely to be successful?

choices.a: No, because only a small amount of city tax funds has been used to maintain the cemetery.
choices.b: No, because the ordinance does not violate the establishment clause of the First Amendment.
choices.c: Yes, because city maintenance of any religious object is a violation of the establishment clause of the First Amendment.
choices.d: Yes, because no compelling governmental interest justifies authorizing private persons to erect religious monuments or markers in a city-operated cemetery.

一个城市根据一项城市条例运营一个公墓。该条例要求，城市公墓的运营主要由向个人出售墓地所得的收入来支持。该条例进一步规定，购买墓地使所有者有权获得该墓地的永久性维护，并有权自费在墓地上建立其所选择的纪念碑或标记物，但需遵守一定的尺寸限制。该城市条例要求市政府维护公墓，包括修剪草坪、浇灌花卉和清除积雪，并规定如果出售墓地的收入不足，则动用城市税款进行此类维护。

尽管墓地以完全公平市价出售（其中包括永久性维护的现值），但近年来出售此类墓地的收入已不足以维护该公墓。因此，一小部分城市税款也被用于此目的。

一群城市纳税人对该市提起诉讼，就城市条例允许墓地所有者在其墓地上建立宗教纪念碑或标记物的规定，对其合宪性提出质疑。

这项诉讼有可能成功吗？
options:
A. No, because only a small amount of city tax funds has been used to maintain the cemetery.
不会，因为只有一小部分城市税款被用于维护公墓。

B. No, because the ordinance does not violate the establishment clause of the First Amendment.
不会，因为该条例没有违反第一修正案的国教条款。

C. Yes, because city maintenance of any religious object is a violation of the establishment clause of the First Amendment.
会，因为市政府对任何宗教物品的维护都违反了第一修正案的国教条款。

D. Yes, because no compelling governmental interest justifies authorizing private persons to erect religious monuments or markers in a city-operated cemetery.
会，因为没有任何强制性的政府利益能够成为授权私人在市政府运营的公墓中建立宗教纪念碑或标记物的正当理由。
data.explanation:
City taxpayers have challenged the constitutionality of a city ordinance that permits persons to erect religious monuments or markers on cemetery lots maintained by the city. This challenge triggers the First Amendment establishment clause since it alleges that the government failed to remain neutral toward religion. As a result, the government action will be reviewed under the historical test and upheld if the action has historically been permitted in accordance with the original meaning of the Constitution.

Historically, individuals have had the right to erect monuments or markers of their choice on individual cemetery lots, including religious monuments or markers on lots in city-operated cemeteries. And since the ordinance here adheres to this long-standing practice, it is in accord with the original meaning of the Constitution and does not violate the establishment clause (Choice C). As a result, the taxpayers' suit will likely be unsuccessful.

(Choice A) The small amount of city tax funds used to maintain the cemetery helps establish the lack of government entanglement with religion required to satisfy the Lemon test. But this test has been abandoned in establishment-clause challenges.

(Choice D) The city ordinance would have to be necessary to achieve a compelling government interest to survive strict scrutiny. But courts will only apply this heightened standard and forego the historical test when a law expressly favors or disfavors religion—which the ordinance here did not do. Therefore, no compelling interest is required.

Educational objective:
Establishment clause challenges are reviewed under the historical test, which upholds government actions that have historically been permitted in accordance with the original meaning of the Constitution.



选项正确率统计：A选项 1%，B选项 96%（正确选项），C选项 1%，D选项 0%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

城市纳税人对一项允许个人在市政府维护的墓地上建立宗教纪念碑或标记物的城市条例的合宪性提出质疑。这一质疑触发了第一修正案的国教条款（establishment clause），因为它声称政府未能对宗教保持中立。因此，该政府行为将根据历史测试（historical test）进行审查，如果该行为根据宪法的原意在历史上是被允许的，则该行为将得到维持。

历史上，个人一直有权在个人墓地上建立自己选择的纪念碑或标记物，包括在市立公墓的墓地上建立宗教纪念碑或标记物。由于本案中的条例遵循了这一长期存在的实践，它符合宪法的原意，并未违反国教条款。（选项C）因此，纳税人的诉讼很可能不会成功。

（选项A）用于维护公墓的少量城市税款有助于满足 Lemon test 所要求的缺乏政府与宗教纠葛的条件。但该测试在国教条款的挑战中已被废弃。

（选项D）该城市条例必须是为了实现重大利益所必需，才能通过严格审查。但只有当法律明确地支持或反对宗教时——本案中的条例并未如此——法院才会适用这一更高标准并放弃历史测试。因此，不需要重大利益。

教学目标：
对国教条款的质疑应根据历史测试进行审查，该测试支持那些根据宪法的原意在历史上被允许的政府行为。

References

Kennedy v. Bremerton School Dist., 142 S. Ct. 2407, 2428 (2022) (holding that challenges based on the establishment clause "must be interpreted by reference to historical practices and understandings").

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law Establishment Clause
正确答案：选项 B

不会成功，因为该条例没有违反第一修正案的国教条款 (Establishment Clause)。

本题的核心在于判断政府允许在公有墓地设立私人宗教墓碑，并使用税款维护墓地环境，是否构成政府对宗教的“确立”或“支持”。

⚖️ 法律推理深度解析

1. 历史测试标准 (The Historical Test)

根据最高法院最新的判例（如 Kennedy v. Bremerton School Dist.），对国教条款的审查主要依据历史实践和理解。

历史上，美国一直允许个人在公墓中竖立自己选择的墓碑（包括宗教标志）。这种长期存在的传统表明，这种做法符合宪法原意，并不被视为政府在建立国教。

2. 私人言论 vs. 政府言论

这是一个关键的区别点。墓碑上的十字架或大卫之星是私人言论 (Private Speech)，而不是政府言论。

  • 政府的角色： 仅提供一个中立的场所（公墓）。
  • 个人的角色： 自费购买、选择并竖立墓碑。

当政府仅仅是允许私人表达宗教观点，且对所有观点（宗教或非宗教）一视同仁时，并不违反国教条款。

3. 维护费用的性质

纳税人质疑的焦点在于“税款被用于维护”。然而，市政府修剪草坪、铲雪是维护公共财产 (Public Property) 的一般性义务。

政府并没有出钱修建宗教纪念碑，只是在维护整个墓地的环境。这种“附带受益” (Incidental Benefit) 并不构成违宪的宗教纠葛。

🚫 为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A (错误)

理由：“只用了一小部分钱”。
解析：这是一个事实，但不是法律理由。如果某项行为违宪，哪怕只花了一分钱也是违宪的。本案合宪是因为行为本身的性质，而不是因为花费少。

选项 C (错误)

理由：“维护任何宗教物品都违宪”。
解析：这种说法过于绝对。政府经常为宗教机构提供一般性公共服务（如警察、消防、道路维护），这并不违宪。关键在于政府是否在偏袒或推广宗教。

选项 D (错误)

理由：“没有重大利益 (Compelling Interest)”。
解析：这引用了严格审查 (Strict Scrutiny) 标准。但严格审查通常只在政府行为歧视宗教或明确基于宗教进行分类时才适用。本案中的条例是中立的（允许任何人立碑），因此不需要证明“重大利益”。

🎓 MBE 备考锦囊

在处理 Establishment Clause（国教条款）问题时，请注意区分：

1. Lemon Test (旧标准)：目的、效果、纠葛。虽然在现代判例中逐渐被废弃，但在旧题解析中常出现。

2. Historical Test (新标准)：现在的审查重点是“历史和传统”。如果一项政府行为（如立法会议前的祷告、公墓管理）有悠久的历史传统，它通常是合宪的。

3. 中立性 (Neutrality)：如果政府对宗教言论和非宗教言论一视同仁（例如在公园里允许所有人演讲），通常不会违反国教条款。

© MBE Constitutional Law Review

questions.question:
A city ordinance requires a taxicab operator's license to operate a taxicab in the city. The ordinance states that the sole criteria for the issuance of such a license are driving ability and knowledge of the city's geography. Applicants are tested by the city for these qualifications with detailed questionnaires, written and oral examinations, and practical behind-the-wheel demonstrations.
The ordinance does not limit the number of licenses that may be issued. It does, however, allow any citizen to file an objection to the issuance of a particular license, but only on the ground that an applicant does not possess the required qualifications. City licensing officials are also authorized by the ordinance to determine, in their discretion, whether to hold an evidentiary hearing on an objection before issuing a license.
A woman applies for a taxicab operator's license and is found to be fully qualified after completing the usual licensing process. Her name is then posted as a prospective licensee, subject only to the objection process. A man who is already a licensed taxicab driver files an objection to the issuance of such a license to the woman solely on the ground that the grant of a license to her would impair the value of his existing license. He demands a hearing before a license is issued to the woman so that he may have an opportunity to prove his claim. City licensing officials refuse to hold such a hearing, and they issue a license to the woman.
The man petitions for review of this action by city officials in an appropriate court, alleging that the Constitution requires city licensing officials to grant his request for a hearing before issuing a license to the woman.
For whom should the court rule in this case?

choices.a: City officials, because the licensing ordinance does not give the man any property interest in being free of competition from additional licensees.
choices.b: City officials, because the man had the benefit of the licensing ordinance and, therefore, may not now question actions taken under it.
choices.c: The man, because the determination of whether to hold a hearing may not constitutionally be left to the discretion of the same officials whose action is being challenged.
choices.d: The man, because the due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment requires all persons whose property may be adversely affected by governmental action to be given an opportunity for a hearing before such action occurs.
